or which are approaching so closely on such through highway as to constitute an immediate hazard during the time such driver is moving across or within the intersection.

elements.justification: As in NRS_484B_257_1_o1: x as a member of the admitted traffic aggregate; a dev.human_direction with role police_officer, or a dev.traffic_signal not dev.inoperative, governing x's approach carrier or the intersection (dev.governs).
As in NRS_484B_257_1_o1: a dev.stop_sign or dev.yield_sign governing x's approach carrier or the intersection, at x's entry (drv.motion.entering_region).
'vehicle' is the admitted aggregate; 'the driver' is read through its controlled motion.

'shall yield the right-of-way' (DEF-NRS-484A-210 'to proceed ... in preference to another vehicle'): x does not enter the intersection (drv.motion.entering_region over rel.occupies) while a through-highway vehicle is owed precedence.

'other vehicles' are the admitted aggregate. 'which have entered the intersection from such through highway': y occupies the intersection, having entered it through a carrier (drv.position.entered_via, st.lane_enters) that lies on the through highway (st.on_way 'the public way ... a structure region lies on', of kind st.highway) on which x's approach carrier does not lie.

operationalizations.standard: approaching so closely on the through highway as to constitute an immediate hazard during the time the driver is moving across or within the intersection
operationalizations.convention: Gap acceptance (HCM critical headway for a minor-street crossing or turn): a vehicle on an approach carrier of the intersection lying on the through highway (rel.occupies, st.lane_enters, st.on_way), outside the intersection, is an immediate hazard where its ground distance to the intersection (st.region_geometry) is at most its speed (kin.speed) times p.immediate_hazard_gap; the critical gap stands for the time the subject needs to move across or within the intersection, and the bound moves with the other vehicle's proximity and speed.

applicability: As NRS_484B_257_1_o1: x is a vehicle entering intersection i at this observation (drv.motion.entering_region x i) through an approach carrier c it occupies (st.lane_enters c i); a dev.stop_sign or dev.yield_sign governs c or i; x, a member of traffic (ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic), is not controlled by a dev.human_direction with role police_officer or a dev.traffic_signal that is not dev.inoperative governing c or i. And NRS_484B_257_1_o1 is complied with for x at this observation (rule NRS_484B_257_1_o1 {x -> x}): that rule being engaged at exactly this entry, its compliance is the fact the words refer to, that x stopped, or under a yield sign slowed or stopped, on this approach.
obligation: At this entry, for every highway h2 (st.highway) on which i lies and c does not (st.on_way i h2; st.on_way c h2 false), no vehicle y other than x (ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle) either (1) occupies i, having entered it through a carrier c2 that lies on h2 (drv.position.entered_via y i c2, st.lane_enters c2 i, st.on_way c2 h2), or (2) occupies an approach carrier c2 of i lying on h2 (rel.occupies y c2, st.lane_enters c2 i, st.on_way c2 h2), does not occupy i, and st_region_geometry_distance y i is at most kin_speed y times p.immediate_hazard_gap.

narrowings.why: Control of traffic is read as control of x's own approach or intersection; officer and signal presence are read as their status.
'proper signs' are read through the presence of a stop or yield sign.
'the driver' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion.
The yield is judged at x's entry into the intersection.

'during the time such driver is moving across or within the intersection' is read through the critical gap, not through a prediction of x's own crossing time; 'such through highway' is a highway the intersection lies on and x's signed approach does not.

segmentation.text: The driver of a vehicle
about to enter or exit a controlled-access highway
shall yield the right-of-way
to all vehicles approaching on the highway
whose proximity constitutes an immediate hazard
and shall continue to yield the right-of-way
to that traffic
until the driver may proceed with reasonable safety.

elements.justification: 'vehicle' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle; 'the driver' is read through its controlled motion.

'a controlled-access highway' is st.controlled_access 'a highway with access only at designated points' (DEF-NRS-484A-060 'no legal right of access except at such points only'). 'about to enter or exit' is read by the movement it leads to: the footprint beginning to overlap the region (drv.motion.entering_region) or ceasing to (drv.motion.leaving_region), through rel.occupies.
'shall yield the right-of-way' (DEF-NRS-484A-210 'to proceed ... in preference'): x does not make the entry or the exit while a vehicle owed precedence is a hazard.

'all vehicles' are the admitted aggregate; 'approaching on the highway': y occupies the controlled-access region (rel.occupies) and is moving (drv.motion.moving over kin.speed); its approach toward x is read by the standard's closest approach.

operationalizations.standard: proximity that constitutes an immediate hazard

about to enter or exit a controlled-access highway
shall yield the right-of-way

to that traffic
until the driver may proceed with reasonable safety.

elements.justification: 'vehicle' is the admitted aggregate; 'the driver' is read through its controlled motion.
As in NRS_484B_263_o1: st.controlled_access 'a highway with access only at designated points'; entry and exit read by drv.motion.entering_region and drv.motion.leaving_region over rel.occupies.

'that traffic' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic, referring back to the vehicles approaching on the highway; each such vehicle is read as a member ('vehicles ... using any highway for purposes of travel').

operationalizations.standard: proceed with reasonable safety
operationalizations.convention: Safe merge headway (two-second rule, HCM freeway merge gap acceptance): at the entry or exit, every approaching vehicle of that traffic (prim.closest_approach_within over the critical-gap horizon) is at a surface gap from x (rel.surface_gap 'distance between the nearest points of two bodies') of at least its own speed (kin.speed) times p.merge_time_headway, so the margin grows with the approaching vehicle's speed.

segmentation.text: A pedestrian
walking or otherwise traveling on a sidewalk
who encounters an obstruction to his or her mobility on the sidewalk,
including, without limitation, a short section of the sidewalk that is missing or impassable,
may proceed
with due care
on the immediately adjacent highway to move around such an obstruction.
Such a pedestrian:
(a) Must walk or otherwise travel as far to the side of the highway near the sidewalk
as possible;
(b) May walk or otherwise travel on the highway in the direction he or she was walking or traveling on the sidewalk, regardless of the direction of traffic;
(c) May walk or otherwise travel in a lane provided for bicycles, electric bicycles or electric scooters
if the area between the lane and the sidewalk is impassable;
and
(d) Must return to the sidewalk
as soon as practicable.

elements.justification: 'pedestrian' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-165::pedestrian ('a person afoot, a person in a manual or motorized wheelchair, or a person on an electric personal assistive mobility device').

'walking or otherwise traveling on a sidewalk': rel.occupies 'a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region' of a st.sidewalk ('area for pedestrians between roadway and property line'; DEF-NRS-484A-240), while moving (drv.motion.moving). st.sidewalk is not a stand-in for a crosswalk.

'encounters an obstruction to his or her mobility on the sidewalk': a st.obstruction ('a physical object on or beside the roadway that is not a road user', kinds including sidewalk_fixture, barrier, excavation) within the encounter reach of the pedestrian (st.region_geometry 'the ground distance from a road user's body outline to it') while the pedestrian is on the sidewalk.

'a short section of the sidewalk that is missing or impassable' is no object: st.obstruction ('a physical object ... that is not a road user') covers a blocked section only; a missing or impassable stretch of sidewalk has no atom. Mapped to the nearest atoms with a gap.

'may proceed': the pedestrian moves (drv.motion.moving) while on the highway (st.highway 'the entire public way between its boundary lines', which the sidewalk lies on, st.on_way) and off every sidewalk (rel.occupies); the duty of care binds that proceeding.

'on the immediately adjacent highway': the pedestrian occupies the highway the sidewalk it left lies on (st.on_way) and no sidewalk (rel.occupies); st.highway is not a stand-in for the roadway, and any part of the way off the sidewalk counts. 'to move around such an obstruction' is a purpose, read through the pedestrian having left the sidewalk where it encountered the obstruction and having stayed off it since.
'Such a pedestrian' refers back to the pedestrian of the admitted aggregate in the situation s2 to s7 describe.

operationalizations.standard: due care
operationalizations.convention: Surrogate safety conflict (FHWA SSAM): while proceeding on the highway, the pedestrian creates no predicted conflict: no other road user's centre is predicted, under constant velocities, to come within p.conflict_clearance of the pedestrian's within p.immediate_hazard_gap. Due care is a standard of care, so the reading is a surrogate.

residues.why: A permission to travel against the direction of traffic; no duty of this node concerns the pedestrian's direction, so the duty is the same whichever way the pedestrian walks.

applicability: x is a pedestrian (ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-165::pedestrian) on the highway beside a sidewalk it left at an obstruction: for a sidewalk w (st.sidewalk) and a highway h (st.highway) with st.on_way w h, x occupies h and no sidewalk at this observation, and has done so at every observation since an observation at which x occupied w, was moving (drv.motion.moving x with p.speed_resolution) and was within p.obstruction_encounter_reach of an obstruction o (st.obstruction; st_region_geometry_distance x o).
obligation: Where x is moving (drv.motion.moving x with p.speed_resolution), no road user z other than x is in predicted conflict with x: not both prim.closest_approach_within x z with horizon p.immediate_hazard_gap and prim.closest_approach_distance x z with the same horizon below p.conflict_clearance.

narrowings.why: The permission is read as the duty of care that binds the proceeding it permits; where the pedestrian is not moving no proceeding is judged.
'to move around such an obstruction' is read through the conduct: leaving the sidewalk where the obstruction was encountered and staying off it since.

shall yield
the right-of-way
to any person riding a bicycle, an electric bicycle or an electric scooter
or a pedestrian
as provided in subsection 6 of NRS 484B.297 [NRS-484B-297-6]

a pathway or lane provided for bicycles, electric bicycles or electric scooters

'a pedestrian' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-165::pedestrian, limited by s6 to one in the situation of NRS 484B.297(6).

applicability: x is a motor vehicle (ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-130::motor_vehicle), moving (drv.motion.moving x with p.speed_resolution) with its footprint on a bicycle lane or path b (st.bicycle_lane_or_path; rel.occupies x b).

The yield is judged at every observation at which x moves on the bicycle lane or path; a halted x proceeds in preference to no one.

segmentation.text: The driver of a motor vehicle
shall yield
the right-of-way
to any person riding a bicycle, an electric bicycle or an electric scooter
or a pedestrian
as provided in subsection 6 of NRS 484B.297 [NRS-484B-297-6]
on the pathway or lane.
The driver of a motor vehicle
shall not enter, stop, stand, park or drive within
a pathway or lane provided for bicycles, electric bicycles or electric scooters
except: (a) When entering or exiting an alley or driveway;
(b) When operating or parking a disabled vehicle;
(c) To avoid conflict with other traffic;
(d) In the performance of official duties;
(e) In compliance with the directions of a police officer;
or
(f) In an emergency.

elements.justification: 'motor vehicle' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-130::motor_vehicle; 'the driver' is read through its controlled motion.

'enter' is drv.motion.entering_region; 'stop' (prohibited: DEF-NRS-484A-260 'any halting, even momentarily'), 'stand' (DEF-NRS-484A-250 'the halting of a vehicle') and 'park' (DEF-NRS-484A-155 'the standing of a vehicle') are halts, drv.motion.halted; 'drive within' is moving (drv.motion.moving) with the footprint on the lane (rel.occupies). Together they cover every observation at which x's footprint overlaps the lane.

'a pathway or lane provided for bicycles, electric bicycles or electric scooters' is st.bicycle_lane_or_path 'lane or separate path reserved for bicycles and the devices a jurisdiction groups with them'; the place word keeps its whole extent.

'When entering or exiting an alley or driveway': x moving (drv.motion.moving) within the access reach (st.region_geometry distance) of a st.driveway_or_alley_entrance ('private road, alley or driveway meeting the highway'; DEF-NRS-484A-190 'Private way or driveway'). The kind does not tell an alley's entrance from a driveway's, and both are named, so its exclusion does not apply.

'a disabled vehicle': no atom carries a vehicle's inability to move under its own power; sig.hazard ('both indicators flashing together') and kin.engine_running (not a stand-in for motion) are the nearest evidence and do not denote it: gap.

'To avoid conflict with other traffic': a purpose, read through the conduct it explains: x's current overlap of the bicycle lane or path began (drv.motion.entering_region) at an observation at which another member of the admitted traffic aggregate was in predicted conflict with x (prim.closest_approach_within and prim.closest_approach_distance, the same conflict bound as elsewhere in this run).

'In the performance of official duties': a purpose, read through the vehicle's official or emergency class (ru.official_vehicle 'a vehicle in official or contracted road service, identifiable by livery or equipment'; ru.emergency_vehicle). Neither is read as a responding emergency vehicle, which the exception does not require.

'In compliance with the directions of a police officer': a dev.human_direction ('a person directing traffic and the direction given') with role police_officer governing (dev.governs) a travel region x occupies (st.travel_region, rel.occupies) or the bicycle lane itself.

'In an emergency': no atom carries an emergency situation; sig.hazard and ru.emergency_vehicle ('Not a stand-in for: a responding emergency vehicle') are the nearest evidence and do not denote it: gap.

applicability: x is a motor vehicle (ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-130::motor_vehicle) and none of the exceptions holds at this observation: (a) x is moving (drv.motion.moving x with p.speed_resolution) within p.access_crossing_reach of a st.driveway_or_alley_entrance (st_region_geometry_distance); (b) x is disabled (nearest atoms sig.hazard, kin.engine_running; gap proposed); (c) x's current overlap of a bicycle lane or path b began (drv.motion.entering_region x b, every observation since with rel.occupies x b) at an observation at which some road user z other than x, a member of traffic (ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic) not on b, was in predicted conflict with x (prim.closest_approach_within x z with horizon p.immediate_hazard_gap and prim.closest_approach_distance x z below p.conflict_clearance); (d) x is a ru.official_vehicle or a ru.emergency_vehicle; (e) a dev.human_direction with role police_officer governs (dev.governs) a travel region x occupies; (f) an emergency (nearest atoms sig.hazard, ru.emergency_vehicle; gap proposed). This applicability, exceptions included, is what NRS_484B_270_4 composes.
obligation: x's footprint overlaps no bicycle lane or path (rel.occupies x b false for every b of kind st.bicycle_lane_or_path): whether entering it (drv.motion.entering_region), halted on it (drv.motion.halted with p.speed_resolution) or moving within it (drv.motion.moving).

narrowings.why: 'the driver' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion.

Every halt on the lane is read as forbidden: 'stop' (DEF-NRS-484A-260) excepts halts to avoid conflict or on an officer's or a device's direction, 'stand' excepts halts receiving or discharging passengers, and only a halt that is both is covered by neither word; such a halt is read as forbidden too.
The purpose of avoiding conflict is read through a predicted conflict with other traffic at the observation x moved onto the lane.
The performance of official duties is read through the vehicle's official or emergency class.
The officer's role and direction are read through the dev.human_direction present and governing.

segmentation.text: Except as otherwise provided in subsection 3 [NRS-484B-270-3],
the driver of a motor vehicle
shall not enter or proceed through an intersection
while driving within a pathway or lane provided for bicycles, electric bicycles or electric scooters.

elements.justification: 'motor vehicle' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-130::motor_vehicle; 'the driver' is read through its controlled motion.

'shall not enter or proceed through an intersection': x's footprint does not overlap a st.intersection ('the region where two roadways meet'; DEF-NRS-484A-105), neither on entering it (drv.motion.entering_region) nor while proceeding through it (rel.occupies). st.intersection is not a stand-in for a crosswalk or stop line.

'while driving within a pathway or lane provided for bicycles ...': x moving (drv.motion.moving) with its footprint on a st.bicycle_lane_or_path ('lane or separate path reserved for bicycles and the devices a jurisdiction groups with them'), at the same observation.

applicability: x is a motor vehicle (ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-130::motor_vehicle), moving (drv.motion.moving x with p.speed_resolution) with its footprint on a bicycle lane or path b (st.bicycle_lane_or_path; rel.occupies x b), and NRS_484B_270_3_o2 applies to x at this observation (ruleApplies NRS_484B_270_3_o2 {x -> x}): its applicability holds exactly where none of the exceptions (a) to (f) of subsection 3 holds, which is what 'except as otherwise provided in subsection 3' leaves this duty to.
obligation: x's footprint overlaps no intersection at this observation (rel.occupies x i false for every i of kind st.intersection): x neither enters one (drv.motion.entering_region) nor proceeds through it.

narrowings.why: 'the driver' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion.

contract: Road user x is overtaking road user y alongside at the observation: the side-by-side phase of an overtaking, on either side of y. It holds where their headings are aligned (rel.same_direction, with aligned_cosine as the relation's tolerance), their bodies overlap along x's heading (rel.longitudinal_overlap positive), and x's speed exceeds y's (kin.speed, m/s) by more than speed_margin, the speed resolution below which the two count as keeping pace. Either side of y counts. Not denoted: the approach from behind or the return ahead of y, the side on which x passes, where either body is on the road, a lane change, contact, or the clearance between the bodies.

params.name: aligned_cosine
params.meaning: the tolerance of rel.same_direction: the cosine of the largest angle between the two headings that still counts as travelling the same way

params.name: speed_margin
params.meaning: the speed resolution of a speed difference: the smallest excess of x's speed over y's that counts as gaining on y rather than keeping pace

elements.span: their headings are aligned (rel.same_direction, with aligned_cosine as the relation's tolerance)
elements.justification: rel.same_direction: "headings aligned: the cosine of the angle between the headings is above its tolerance"; the tolerance is the formal aligned_cosine.

elements.span: their bodies overlap along x's heading (rel.longitudinal_overlap positive)
elements.justification: rel.longitudinal_overlap: "the bodies overlap along the subject's heading (side by side): the length the two footprints' projections on that axis share, negative for the gap between the projections"; a positive value is the side-by-side phase. Not a stand-in for contact or a distance: the concept states neither.

elements.span: x's speed exceeds y's (kin.speed, m/s) by more than speed_margin
elements.justification: kin.speed: "magnitude of velocity", m/s, read for both road users; gaining on y is x's speed above y's by more than the resolution.

scenarios.name: holds
scenarios.narrative: x and y head the same way within aligned_cosine, their footprints share a positive length along x's heading, and x's kin.speed exceeds y's by more than speed_margin: x is overtaking y alongside.

scenarios.name: fails
scenarios.narrative: x follows y in the same lane with a negative rel.longitudinal_overlap (a gap between the projections) at a higher speed: x has not drawn alongside, so the concept does not hold.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: x and y head the same way and x is faster, but the source does not observe rel.longitudinal_overlap: whether they are side by side is unknown.

segmentation.text: The operator of a bicycle, an electric bicycle or an electric scooter
shall not: Overtake and pass a motor vehicle
unless the operator can do so safely without endangering himself or herself or the occupants of the motor vehicle.

elements.justification: The three machines are the admitted aggregates of the definitions that apply: DEF-NRS-484A-025 ("a device propelled by human power upon which a person may ride"), DEF-NRS-484B-017 ("a device upon which a person may ride, having two or three wheels") and DEF-NRS-484B-018 ("a vehicle with handlebars and an electric motor"). ru.aggregate: "membership of a legal aggregate"; each is claimed by its admitted id and never expanded into class atoms. 'The operator of' names who controls the machine, a role and not a membership, read through the machine's controlled motion (observable_reading agency).

Overtaking and passing is the manoeuvre the proposed concept drv.interaction.overtaking_alongside denotes in its side-by-side phase: "Road user x is overtaking road user y alongside at the observation: the side-by-side phase of an overtaking, on either side of y". The words name no side, so the concept counts either side (unlike drv.interaction.passing_on_right). Its atoms rel.same_direction, rel.longitudinal_overlap and kin.speed are claimed as the concept reads them; rel.longitudinal_overlap is 'not a stand-in' for contact or a distance and is used for neither. 'a motor vehicle' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-130::motor_vehicle ("every vehicle which is self-propelled but not operated upon rails"; "does not include an electric bicycle or an electric scooter"), which the road user overtaken, quantified in the rule, must carry; it is never replaced by ru.motor_vehicle.

operationalizations.standard: safely without endangering himself or herself or the occupants of the motor vehicle
operationalizations.convention: Passing-clearance convention for cycles passing motor vehicles (the endangerment of the occupants and of the rider by the vehicle passed): the surface gap between the two bodies while side by side is at least the passing clearance, read by its degree. Surrogate-safety closest-approach convention (the endangerment of the rider by other traffic): no other road user is predicted, under constant velocities within the critical gap, to come nearer the rider than the conflict radius.

applicability: x carries ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-025::bicycle, ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484B-017::electric_bicycle or ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484B-018::electric_scooter, and at the observation some road user y other than x that carries ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-130::motor_vehicle is being overtaken alongside by x (drv.interaction.overtaking_alongside(x, y) with p.same_direction_cosine and p.overtaking_speed_margin).
obligation: For every road user y other than x that carries ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-130::motor_vehicle and that x is overtaking alongside at the observation: the surface gap between x and y (rel.surface_gap) is at least p.passing_lateral_clearance; and for every road user z other than x and y it is not the case that x and z approach each other within p.immediate_hazard_gap (prim.closest_approach_within) with a closest-approach centre distance (prim.closest_approach_distance) below p.conflict_clearance.

narrowings.why: 'The operator' is read through the machine's controlled motion: the duty binds the conduct of the bicycle, electric bicycle or electric scooter whoever controls it.

'Overtake and pass' is judged in its side-by-side phase, where the clearance to the vehicle passed and the exposure to other traffic arise; the approach from behind and the return ahead are not judged on their own.

'safely without endangering himself or herself or the occupants of the motor vehicle' is read through two contracts only: the surface gap kept to the motor vehicle passed (the exposure of its occupants and of the rider to that vehicle) and the predicted closest approach to every other road user (the rider's exposure to other traffic). The road surface, the sight available and the rider's balance are not read.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: x (ru.bicycle) travels with rel.same_direction to a passenger car y (ru.motor_vehicle), rel.longitudinal_overlap positive and x's kin.speed above y's by more than p.overtaking_speed_margin, with rel.surface_gap between them below p.passing_lateral_clearance; no other road user is in the scene.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: The same overtaking alongside with rel.surface_gap above p.passing_lateral_clearance and no other road user in the scene: the duty binds x alone and is met.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: x (ru.bicycle) rides behind car y in the same lane with a negative rel.longitudinal_overlap and never draws alongside: no overtaking takes place.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: x rides faster than car y in the same direction close beside it, but the source does not observe rel.longitudinal_overlap: whether x is overtaking alongside is unknown.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: x (ru.electric_scooter) overtakes car y alongside with rel.surface_gap above p.passing_lateral_clearance, but an oncoming ru.motor_vehicle z satisfies prim.closest_approach_within with x over p.immediate_hazard_gap at a prim.closest_approach_distance below p.conflict_clearance.

param_proposals.convention: Heading alignment tolerance: the cosine of the largest angle between two headings that still counts as travelling the same way.
param_proposals.source: heading-alignment conventions of trajectory analysis

param_proposals.convention: Speed resolution of a speed difference: the smallest excess of the subject's speed over the other's that counts as gaining on it rather than keeping pace.

param_proposals.source: three-foot passing-clearance statutes and AASHTO Guide for the Development of Bicycle Facilities

param_proposals.convention: Conflict radius: the centre distance at predicted closest approach below which two road users' paths count as in conflict; about the half-length plus half-width of two passenger cars.
param_proposals.source: surrogate safety measures (closest-approach conflict radius)

param_proposals.convention: Critical gap: the time within which another road user's arrival at the conflict area, or its predicted closest approach, counts as an immediate hazard to a road user about to cross or join its path.
param_proposals.source: Highway Capacity Manual critical-gap values

segmentation.text: Where the signal is a steady red with a green turn arrow:
Except as otherwise provided in paragraph (b) [NRS-484B-307-9b],
vehicular traffic
facing the signal
may enter the intersection
only to make the movement indicated by the green turn arrow,
but must yield the right-of-way
to pedestrians lawfully within an adjacent crosswalk and to other traffic lawfully using the intersection.
Drivers turning in the direction of the arrow are thereby advised that so long as the turn arrow is illuminated, oncoming or opposing traffic simultaneously faces a steady red signal.

elements.justification: dev.traffic_signal: "a signal head; state ∈ {circular_green, circular_yellow, circular_red, green_arrow(dir), ...}" and "several states may be displayed at once": a steady red with a green turn arrow is a head displaying circular_red together with green_arrow(dir), dir left or right. 'The signal' is the head tied to the subject's approach in span b4. No 'not a stand-in' clause applies.

'traffic' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic ("pedestrians, ridden or herded animals, vehicles and other conveyances either singly or together using any highway for purposes of travel"). The law's own qualifier 'vehicular' leaves out the members that are not conveyances: pedestrians ("a person afoot, a person in a manual or motorized wheelchair", the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-165::pedestrian, which the rule requires the subject not to carry) and ridden or herded animals, for which the ontology has no class and nothing is read. Cycles and scooters stay in, as 'other conveyances'; paragraph (b) is written as an exception for them, which confirms they are vehicular traffic here.

Facing the signal is the signal governing the approach the subject enters through. dev.governs: "the travel regions whose traffic the device controls ... or an intersection, read as control of the junction itself"; st.lane_enters: "the intersection region a directed approach carrier runs into at its entrance end"; drv.position.entered_via (proposed this iteration): "x is inside region r on its current entry and came in through region c". The approach carrier c is the one x occupied at its entry with st.lane_enters(c, i); the signal governs c or i. dev.governs is 'not a stand-in' for a position and is not used as one.

drv.motion.entering_region (proposed this iteration): "Road user x enters structure region r at the observation: its footprint overlaps r (rel.occupies) at the observation and did not at the observation before"; r is the st.intersection, "the region where two roadways meet".

The movement made through the intersection is read at x's leaving of it (drv.motion.leaving_region: "its footprint overlapped r (rel.occupies) at the observation before and does not overlap it at the observation") by drv.motion.heading_change_since_entry: "The signed heading change of road user x since its footprint last began to overlap region r, in degrees, left positive", integrated from kin.yaw_rate. A left arrow indicates a change of at least the turn recognition angle to the left, a right arrow one to the right. The concept is 'not' a turn by itself; the rule compares it with its own bound.

residues.why: An advisory to drivers turning with the arrow about what opposing traffic faces at the same time; it permits, requires and forbids nothing, and no rule reads it.

applicability: x carries ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic and does not carry ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-165::pedestrian; at the observation x leaves an intersection i (drv.motion.leaving_region(x, i)); at the observation of its latest entry into i (drv.motion.entering_region(x, i), read through a past operator) x came in through a carrier c with st.lane_enters(c, i) (drv.position.entered_via(x, i, c)), and a traffic signal s that governs c or i (dev.governs) displayed circular_red together with green_arrow(d), d left or right. Not engaged where NRS_484B_307_9b_o1 applies to x (composition, exception).
obligation: At that leaving observation the heading change of x since that entry (drv.motion.heading_change_since_entry(x, i) with step p.heading_since_step_carla_scene_graph) shows the movement a green arrow displayed at the entry indicates: at least p.turn_recognition_angle where d is left, at most minus p.turn_recognition_angle where d is right. Where arrows of both directions were displayed, the movement either indicates complies.

narrowings.why: The movement indicated by the arrow is read as the side and the size of the heading change through the intersection, judged when the subject leaves it: a passage turning at least the turn recognition angle toward the arrow's side complies, whatever lane it exits into.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: x (ru.motor_vehicle) enters intersection i from lane c that a signal s governs; s displays circular_red with green_arrow(left) at the entry; x crosses i and leaves it with a heading change since entry well inside p.turn_recognition_angle (straight through).

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: The same entry under circular_red with green_arrow(left); x leaves i with a heading change since entry above p.turn_recognition_angle to the left.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: s displays circular_green at x's entry into i; x crosses straight through.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: x enters i from lane c and crosses straight through, but the source does not observe s's state at the entry.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: x is a ru.bicycle; it enters i under circular_red with green_arrow(left) and leaves straight through: paragraph (b) applies (NRS_484B_307_9b_o1 engaged), so this duty does not.

param_proposals.name: p.turn_recognition_angle
param_proposals.convention: Turn recognition: the heading change through an intersection beyond which a passage counts as a turn rather than a straight crossing; half the right angle of a turn at a right-angled junction, leaving room for skewed junctions and lane offsets.
param_proposals.source: intersection geometry design conventions (AASHTO Green Book)

vehicular traffic
facing the signal
may enter the intersection
only to make the movement indicated by the green turn arrow,
but must yield the right-of-way
to pedestrians lawfully within an adjacent crosswalk and to other traffic lawfully using the intersection.
Drivers turning in the direction of the arrow are thereby advised that so long as the turn arrow is illuminated, oncoming or opposing traffic simultaneously faces a steady red signal.

elements.justification: dev.traffic_signal: "a signal head; state ∈ {circular_green, circular_yellow, circular_red, green_arrow(dir), ...}" and "several states may be displayed at once": a steady red with a green turn arrow is a head displaying circular_red together with green_arrow(dir), dir left or right. No 'not a stand-in' clause applies.

'traffic' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic ("pedestrians, ridden or herded animals, vehicles and other conveyances"). The qualifier 'vehicular' leaves out pedestrians (DEF-NRS-484A-165::pedestrian, "a person afoot", which the subject must not carry) and ridden or herded animals, which have no class atom; cycles and scooters stay in as 'other conveyances'.

Facing the signal is the signal governing the approach the subject enters through: dev.governs ("the travel regions whose traffic the device controls ... or an intersection") on the carrier c with st.lane_enters(c, i) ("the intersection region a directed approach carrier runs into at its entrance end") that x came in through (drv.position.entered_via: "x is inside region r on its current entry and came in through region c"), or on i itself.
drv.motion.entering_region: "its footprint overlaps r (rel.occupies) at the observation and did not at the observation before", r the st.intersection.

The parties yielded to. 'pedestrians' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-165::pedestrian ("a person afoot, a person in a manual or motorized wheelchair"); 'within an adjacent crosswalk' is the pedestrian's footprint overlapping (rel.occupies) a st.crosswalk ("marked crossing, or the unmarked prolongation of sidewalks at an intersection") adjacent to i: a crosswalk recorded as marking the entrance of a carrier entering i (st.entrance_of: "the carrier whose entrance into an intersection a stop line or a crosswalk marks"; st.lane_enters). Distance is not used for adjacency. 'other traffic' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic, every member other than x; 'using the intersection' is its footprint overlapping i (rel.occupies).

operationalizations.standard: yield the right-of-way: not proceeding where the parties' "direction, speed and proximity" "give rise to the danger of a crash unless one grants precedence to the other" (DEF-NRS-484A-210)
operationalizations.convention: Gap-acceptance and surrogate-safety convention: the subject grants precedence where it does not proceed (it is not moving, drv.motion.moving) while a party is in danger of a crash with it; that danger is their predicted closest approach under constant velocities, within the critical gap, coming nearer than the conflict radius, so direction, speed and proximity all enter the prediction by their degree.

residues.why: An advisory to drivers turning with the arrow about what opposing traffic faces at the same time; it permits, requires and forbids nothing, and no rule reads it.

applicability: x carries ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic and does not carry ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-165::pedestrian; at the observation x occupies an intersection i on a passage whose entry (drv.motion.entering_region(x, i), the latest, read through a past operator) came through a carrier c with st.lane_enters(c, i) (drv.position.entered_via(x, i, c)), and at that entry a traffic signal s that governs c or i (dev.governs) displayed circular_red together with green_arrow(d), d left or right. obligation: Where x is moving at the observation (drv.motion.moving with p.speed_resolution): for every road user p carrying ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-165::pedestrian that occupies a crosswalk w recorded as marking the entrance of some carrier c2 entering i (st.entrance_of(w, c2), st.lane_enters(c2, i)), and for every road user u other than x carrying ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic that occupies i, it is not the case that x and that road user approach within p.immediate_hazard_gap (prim.closest_approach_within) with a closest-approach centre distance (prim.closest_approach_distance) below p.conflict_clearance.

segmentation.text: Where the signal is a steady red with a green turn arrow:
A person driving a motorcycle, moped or
trimobile
or riding a bicycle, an electric bicycle or an electric scooter
facing the signal
may proceed straight through or turn in the direction opposite that indicated by the green turn arrow
if:

(1) The person stops before entering the crosswalk on the nearest side of the intersection where the sign or pavement marking indicates where the stop must be made or, in the absence of any such crosswalk, sign or marking, before entering the intersection;

(2) The person waits for two complete cycles of the lights or lighted arrows of the applicable official traffic-control device and the signal does not change because of a malfunction or because the signal failed to detect the presence of the motorcycle, moped, trimobile, bicycle, electric bicycle or electric scooter;
(3) No other device at the place prohibits the turn, if applicable;
and
(4) The person yields the right-of-way
to pedestrians lawfully within an adjacent crosswalk and to other traffic lawfully using the intersection.

elements.justification: dev.traffic_signal: "a signal head; state ∈ {... circular_red, ... green_arrow(dir) ...}" and "several states may be displayed at once": a steady red with a green turn arrow is circular_red displayed together with green_arrow(dir), dir left or right. No 'not a stand-in' clause applies.

The admitted aggregates DEF-NRS-484A-135::motorcycle ("every motor vehicle equipped with a seat or saddle for the use of the driver and designed to travel on not more than three wheels in contact with the ground") and DEF-NRS-484A-125::moped ("a motor-driven scooter, motor-driven cycle or similar vehicle"), claimed by id and never expanded. 'A person driving' names who controls the machine, read through its controlled motion (observable_reading agency).

The admitted aggregates DEF-NRS-484A-025::bicycle ("a device propelled by human power upon which a person may ride"), DEF-NRS-484B-017::electric_bicycle ("a device upon which a person may ride, having two or three wheels") and DEF-NRS-484B-018::electric_scooter ("a vehicle with handlebars and an electric motor"). 'riding' is read through the machine's controlled motion (observable_reading agency).

Facing the signal is the signal governing the approach the person enters through: dev.governs ("the travel regions whose traffic the device controls ... or an intersection") on the carrier c with st.lane_enters(c, i) ("the intersection region a directed approach carrier runs into at its entrance end") that x came in through (drv.position.entered_via: "x is inside region r on its current entry and came in through region c"), or on i itself. dev.governs is 'not a stand-in' for a position and is not used as one.

Proceeding through the intersection is the passage from x's entry (drv.motion.entering_region: "its footprint overlaps r (rel.occupies) at the observation and did not at the observation before") to its leaving (drv.motion.leaving_region). Straight through or a turn opposite the arrow is read at the leaving by drv.motion.heading_change_since_entry ("The signed heading change of road user x since its footprint last began to overlap region r, in degrees, left positive", from kin.yaw_rate): straight where its size stays below the turn recognition angle, opposite where it reaches that angle on the side away from the arrow.

'stops', a stop required, takes DEF-NRS-484A-255 ("complete cessation from movement"): drv.motion.halted (kin.speed at or below the resolution). The places: the pavement marking indicating where the stop must be made is a st.stop_line ("the transverse line marking where vehicles halt for a device") recorded as marking x's approach carrier c (st.entrance_of: "exactly that carrier's entrance, the line or crossing a vehicle approaching through that carrier halts at or before"); the crosswalk on the nearest side is a st.crosswalk recorded as marking c; failing both, the entrance end of c at the st.intersection (st.lane_enters). Before entering is read along c's designated direction (prim.region_offset_along) with the distance to the place (st.region_geometry) within the stop-point tolerance, and the footprint not yet overlapping the crosswalk or the intersection (rel.occupies). st.intersection is 'not a stand-in' for a crosswalk or a stop line: each place is read on its own.

residues.why: Every trimobile, a motor vehicle with a seat designed to travel on three wheels, is already a member of the motorcycle aggregate claimed on span c2, whose definition takes "every motor vehicle equipped with a seat or saddle for the use of the driver and designed to travel on not more than three wheels in contact with the ground": the duty is the same whether or not the word is read.

applicability: x carries ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-135::motorcycle, ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-125::moped, ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-025::bicycle, ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484B-017::electric_bicycle or ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484B-018::electric_scooter; at the observation x leaves an intersection i (drv.motion.leaving_region(x, i)); at the observation of its latest entry into i (drv.motion.entering_region(x, i), read through a past operator) x came in through a carrier c with st.lane_enters(c, i) (drv.position.entered_via(x, i, c)) and a traffic signal s that governs c or i (dev.governs) displayed circular_red together with green_arrow(d), d left or right; and at the leaving observation the heading change since that entry (drv.motion.heading_change_since_entry(x, i) with step p.heading_since_step_carla_scene_graph) shows a straight-through passage (its absolute value below p.turn_recognition_angle) or a turn opposite d (at most minus p.turn_recognition_angle where d is left, at least p.turn_recognition_angle where d is right).
obligation: A halt before the entry, searched in the past (the approach convention). Event: x's entry into i that the applicability names, made through carrier c (the carrier x occupied at the observation before the entry with st.lane_enters(c, i)). Place, in order: a stop line recorded as marking c (st.entrance_of(line, c)); where c's marks are observed and include no stop line, a crosswalk recorded as marking c; where neither is recorded for c, the entrance end of c at i. Act: an observation at which x is halted (drv.motion.halted with p.speed_resolution) while occupying c, its body within p.stop_point_tolerance of the place (st.region_geometry distance), not past it along c's designated direction (prim.region_offset_along of the place from x not negative), and its footprint overlapping neither i nor, where the place is a crosswalk, that crosswalk. Search: back from the entry, ending at the approach start (the last observation before the entry at which x, on c, is outside the place's stopping zone upstream: off the mark, short of it and farther from it than p.stop_point_tolerance) or at x's previous entry into i through the same place; nothing else ends it. Verdict: complied where the search finds the act; violated where it reaches either end without it; unknown only where it reaches neither (the recording begins inside the approach) or where c's association with a mark, c's direction or x's place relative to the mark is unobserved and the verdict turns on it. Judged at the leaving observation, the search running from the entry.

narrowings.why: 'A person driving' is read through the machine's controlled motion: the duty binds the motorcycle's or moped's conduct whoever controls it.
'riding' is read through the machine's controlled motion: the duty binds the conduct of the bicycle, electric bicycle or electric scooter whoever rides it.

The places are read in the order the words give them under the ontology's approach convention: the pavement marking indicating where the stop must be made is the stop line marking the approach; failing one, the crosswalk on the near side is the crosswalk marking the approach; failing both, the entrance of the intersection. A sign that indicates a stopping point without a line is not carried by any atom and is not read.

scenarios.narrative: x (ru.motorcycle) approaches i on lane c, which a stop line marks (st.entrance_of); it never halts on c, enters i while s governing c displays circular_red with green_arrow(left), and leaves straight through. scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: x (ru.bicycle) halts on c within p.stop_point_tolerance of the stop line marking c, short of it, then enters i under circular_red with green_arrow(left) and leaves straight through.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: x (ru.motorcycle) enters i while s displays circular_green and leaves straight through.

scenarios.name: blind

scenarios.narrative: x's recording begins with x already on c inside the stopping zone of the stop line, rolling slowly; no halt is recorded before it enters i under circular_red with green_arrow(left) and leaves straight through. The search reaches neither the approach start nor a previous entry.

obligation: Read at the observation of x's latest entry into i, through a past operator from the leaving observation. 'riding' is read through the machine's controlled motion.
'the applicable official traffic-control device' is the signal head governing the person's approach; its presence on the road is read as the evidence of its official status.

The passage from x's entry into i to its leaving; straight through or opposite the arrow read at the leaving by drv.motion.heading_change_since_entry ("in degrees, left positive", from kin.yaw_rate) against the turn recognition angle.

The parties yielded to. 'pedestrians' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-165::pedestrian ("a person afoot, a person in a manual or motorized wheelchair"); 'within an adjacent crosswalk' is the pedestrian's footprint overlapping (rel.occupies) a st.crosswalk recorded as marking the entrance of a carrier entering i (st.entrance_of: "the carrier whose entrance into an intersection a stop line or a crosswalk marks"; st.lane_enters). Distance is not used for adjacency. 'other traffic' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic ("pedestrians, ridden or herded animals, vehicles and other conveyances"), every member other than x; 'using the intersection' is its footprint overlapping i (rel.occupies).

operationalizations.standard: yields the right-of-way: not proceeding where the parties' "direction, speed and proximity" "give rise to the danger of a crash unless one grants precedence to the other" (DEF-NRS-484A-210)
operationalizations.convention: Gap-acceptance and surrogate-safety convention: the person grants precedence where they do not proceed (not moving, drv.motion.moving) while a party is in danger of a crash with them; that danger is the predicted closest approach under constant velocities, within the critical gap, coming nearer than the conflict radius, so direction, speed and proximity all enter the prediction by their degree.

residues.why: Every trimobile, a motor vehicle with a seat designed to travel on three wheels, is already a member of the motorcycle aggregate claimed on span c2 ("every motor vehicle equipped with a seat or saddle for the use of the driver and designed to travel on not more than three wheels in contact with the ground"): the duty is the same whether or not the word is read.

applicability: As NRS_484B_307_9b_o1: x carries one of the five aggregates of spans c2 and c4; at the observation x leaves intersection i (drv.motion.leaving_region(x, i)); at its latest entry into i (read through a past operator) it came in through carrier c with st.lane_enters(c, i) (drv.position.entered_via(x, i, c)) while a traffic signal s that governs c or i (dev.governs) displayed circular_red together with green_arrow(d), d left or right; and at the leaving the heading change since that entry (drv.motion.heading_change_since_entry(x, i) with step p.heading_since_step_carla_scene_graph) shows a straight-through passage (absolute value below p.turn_recognition_angle) or a turn opposite d.
obligation: At every observation from that entry up to the leaving (read through a past operator from the leaving observation) at which x occupies i and is moving (drv.motion.moving with p.speed_resolution): for every road user p carrying ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-165::pedestrian that occupies a crosswalk w recorded as marking the entrance of some carrier c2 entering i (st.entrance_of(w, c2), st.lane_enters(c2, i)), and for every road user u other than x carrying ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic that occupies i, it is not the case that x and that road user approach within p.immediate_hazard_gap (prim.closest_approach_within) with a closest-approach centre distance (prim.closest_approach_distance) below p.conflict_clearance.

narrowings.why: 'A person driving' is read through the machine's controlled motion.
'riding' is read through the machine's controlled motion.

'lawfully' is not read: every pedestrian in such a crosswalk and every other member of traffic inside the intersection is yielded to. 'an adjacent crosswalk' is read as a crosswalk recorded as marking the entrance of a carrier entering the intersection; a crosswalk across the exit of a one-way leg is not read.

scenarios.name: idle

param_proposals.name: p.speed_resolution
param_proposals.convention: Sensor resolution: the smallest speed the acquisition standard separates from standstill; a speed at or below it counts as no motion.
param_proposals.source: speed resolution of the carla_scene_graph acquisition standard

param_proposals.name: p.immediate_hazard_gap
param_proposals.convention: Critical gap: the time within which another road user's arrival at the conflict area, or its predicted closest approach, counts as an immediate hazard to a road user about to cross or join its path.
param_proposals.source: Highway Capacity Manual critical-gap values

param_proposals.name: p.conflict_clearance
param_proposals.convention: Conflict radius: the centre distance at predicted closest approach below which two road users' paths count as in conflict; about the half-length plus half-width of two passenger cars.
param_proposals.source: surrogate safety measures (closest-approach conflict radius)

param_proposals.name: p.turn_recognition_angle
param_proposals.convention: Turn recognition: the heading change through an intersection beyond which a passage counts as a turn rather than a straight crossing; half the right angle of a turn at a right-angled junction, leaving room for skewed junctions and lane offsets.
param_proposals.source: intersection geometry design conventions (AASHTO Green Book)

contract: Road user x has turned so as to proceed in the opposite direction: the turning that the corpus defines as "the turning of a vehicle upon a highway so as to proceed in the opposite direction, whether accomplished by one continuous movement or not", observed as a reversal of x's heading. It holds at an observation where the absolute value of x's signed heading change over the window behind it (prim.heading_change with window; degrees, left positive) differs from the literal half turn by no more than reversal_tolerance: the heading now points the opposite way within the tolerance, and a heading change that has gone past the half turn by more than the tolerance (a loop back toward the first direction) does not count. A turning made in several movements, forward and backing, counts, since the heading change is integrated through all of them. The act begins within the window behind the observation of recognition; it is recognized at the observation at which this condition rises; it holds at the later observations at which the reversal still lies within the window behind them, which are not the act again, and it ends when the reversal leaves that window. Unknown where the window is truncated, sampled too sparsely, or a yaw rate is missing. Not denoted: a turning by less than a reversal, or the place of the turning: the caller states the highway or the zone.

params.name: window
params.meaning: the longest time over which a reversal of heading, in one movement or several, is recognized as one turning: the window behind the observation over which the heading change is integrated

params.name: reversal_tolerance
params.meaning: the largest difference between the size of the heading change and the half turn within which the road user counts as proceeding in the opposite direction

act.onset: The act begins within the window behind the observation of recognition
act.recognition: it is recognized at the observation at which this condition rises
act.extent: it holds at the later observations at which the reversal still lies within the window behind them, which are not the act again, and it ends when the reversal leaves that window
act.history: Unknown where the window is truncated, sampled too sparsely, or a yaw rate is missing

elements.span: the absolute value of x's signed heading change over the window behind it (prim.heading_change with window; degrees, left positive)
elements.justification: prim.heading_change: "the signed heading change (degrees, left positive) of a road user over the window behind the observation, integrated from kin.yaw_rate; unknown where the window is truncated, sampled too sparsely, or a yaw rate is missing"; its window is the formal window. Integration through forward and backing movements carries "whether accomplished by one continuous movement or not".

residues.why: The place is the caller's: the concept reads x's heading only, and the calling rule states the region (the highway or the zone) the turning is made in.

residues.span: so as to proceed in the opposite direction
residues.why: Read as the reversal of x's own heading. A road user following a bend of the way that itself turns through a half turn within the window also reverses its heading; no atom of the closed set states the course of the way along x's path, so the two are not told apart.

literals.why: the half turn: a heading pointing the opposite way

scenarios.name: holds
scenarios.narrative: x drives along a street, swings left across the centre line and completes the turning heading the opposite way within the window; the size of prim.heading_change differs from the half turn by less than reversal_tolerance.

scenarios.name: fails
scenarios.narrative: x turns right at a junction; the size of prim.heading_change over the window is about a quarter turn.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: x reverses its heading, but its yaw rate is missing during the window.

segmentation.text: The driver of a vehicle
shall not make a U-turn
in an area designated as a school zone or school crossing zone
except:
(a) When there are no children present;
(b) On a day on which school is not in session;
(c) During the period from a half hour after school is no longer in operation to a half hour before school is next in operation;
(d) If the zone is designated by an operational speed limit beacon,
during the hours when the pupils of the school are in class
and the yellow lights of the speed limit beacon are not flashing in the manner which indicates that the speed limit is in effect;
or
(e) If the zone is not designated by an operational speed limit beacon,
during the times when the sign designating the school zone or school crossing zone indicates that the speed limit is not in effect.

As used in this section, “speed limit beacon” means a device which is used in conjunction with a sign and equipped with two or more yellow lights that flash alternately to indicate when the speed limit in a school zone or school crossing zone is in effect.

elements.justification: 'vehicle' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle ("every device in, upon or by which any person or property is or may be transported or drawn upon a highway", with its exceptions), claimed by id. 'The driver of' names who controls it (DEF-NRS-484A-080, "every person who drives or is in actual physical control of a vehicle"), a role read through the vehicle's controlled motion (observable_reading agency), not a membership.

'U-turn' is defined by DEF-NRS-484B-077 ("the turning of a vehicle upon a highway so as to proceed in the opposite direction, whether accomplished by one continuous movement or not"); the proposed definition-born concept drv.motion.u_turn carries it, recognizing the reversal of x's heading over a window through prim.heading_change. The place, upon a highway inside the zone, is stated by span d3.

A school zone or school crossing zone (DEF-NRS-484B-063 "those sections of streets which are adjacent to school property"; DEF-NRS-484B-060) is a legal region class that is also marked on the road; the ontology's section on what is not an atom: "Where the same category is also marked on the road by a sign (dev.zone_sign), the sign is the atom and the category is not." dev.zone_sign: "a sign that begins or ends a signed zone along the road; kind ∈ {school, school_crossing, ...}". The area designated is the travel regions the sign governs (dev.governs: "the travel regions whose traffic the device controls"), and x is in it where its footprint overlaps one (rel.occupies). dev.zone_sign is 'not a stand-in' for whether its condition holds now; that is read only in span d13 through prim.conditions_hold.

Children present in the zone: a road user of class ru.child ("pedestrian who is visibly a child") whose body lies within the presence reach of a travel region the zone sign governs (st.region_geometry: "the ground distance from a road user's body outline to it (zero when they overlap)"), so that children on the sidewalks beside the zone's lanes count. A reach relates the region to the child, not two regions. No children present: no such road user.

The zone designated by a speed limit beacon: a dev.speed_limit_beacon ("a pair or more of yellow lamps mounted with a speed sign, flashing alternately when the sign's limit is in effect", which is the section's own definition in span d14) governing (dev.governs) the travel region x occupies (rel.occupies) or a region the zone sign governs. 'operational' is read through the beacon's presence (observable_reading status).
dev.speed_limit_beacon "flashing attribute": the beacon's lights not flashing in the manner that indicates the limit is in effect is its flashing attribute false.
A zone not designated by a speed limit beacon: no dev.speed_limit_beacon governs (dev.governs) the travel region x occupies or a region the zone sign governs.

The sign designating the zone is the dev.zone_sign of span d3, whose "conditions attribute: a structured reading of the sign's legend" states when its limit is in effect; that it indicates the limit is not in effect is prim.conditions_hold ("the structured conditions of a device ... hold at the observation for a road user") false for x. The sign is 'not a stand-in' for the condition holding, which is why the primitive reads it.

assumptions.meaning: The calendar day of the observation is one on which the school the zone serves is not in session, as declared for the map or the trace.

The time of the observation lies at least a half hour after the school the zone serves last ceased operation and at least a half hour before it next begins operation, as declared for the map or the trace.
The time of the observation lies within the hours during which the pupils of the school the zone serves are in class, as declared for the map or the trace.

residues.why: The section's own definition of a speed limit beacon; dev.speed_limit_beacon's contract ("a pair or more of yellow lamps mounted with a speed sign, flashing alternately when the sign's limit is in effect") already states it, and the elements of spans d8, d10 and d12 read that atom; it imposes no duty of its own.

applicability: x carries ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle; at the observation x's U-turn is recognized (drv.motion.u_turn(x) with p.u_turn_window and p.u_turn_reversal_tolerance rises there); and at some observation of that act (an observation within p.u_turn_window behind the recognition at which x yaws, drv.motion.yawing with p.yaw_rate_resolution) x's footprint overlapped a travel region r governed (dev.governs) by a dev.zone_sign z of kind school or school_crossing that is not an end sign.
obligation: The U-turn is made only where one exception covers the whole act: for one of the alternatives below, that alternative holds at every observation of the act (each observation within p.u_turn_window behind the recognition at which x yaws). (a) No road user of class ru.child lies within p.child_presence_reach (st.region_geometry distance) of a travel region z governs. (b) asm.school_not_in_session_day holds. (c) asm.outside_school_operation_margin holds. (d) A dev.speed_limit_beacon governs the region x occupies or a region z governs, asm.pupils_in_class holds, and that beacon is not flashing. (e) No dev.speed_limit_beacon governs the region x occupies or a region z governs, and z's conditions do not hold for x (prim.conditions_hold false). Where none of them covers the whole act, the duty is violated.

narrowings.why: 'The driver of a vehicle' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion: the duty binds the vehicle's conduct whoever or whatever controls it.
'an area designated as a school zone or school crossing zone' is read through the zone sign on the road and the travel regions it governs; the designation is presumed from the sign's presence.
'operational' is read through the beacon's presence governing the zone's regions; a beacon that is installed but out of order is not told apart.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: x (ru.motor_vehicle) makes a U-turn on a lane governed by a school zone sign z; a ru.child stands within p.child_presence_reach of z's lane at every observation, asm.school_not_in_session_day and asm.outside_school_operation_margin are declared false, and a speed limit beacon governing the lane is flashing.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: x makes a U-turn on a street no school zone or school crossing zone sign governs.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: x drives along z's lane with children on the sidewalk and turns about, but its yaw rate is missing, so whether a U-turn was made is unknown.

scenarios.name: occasion_d3
scenarios.narrative: Baseline as in forbid (children present, school in session, inside the operation margin, beacon flashing): x begins its U-turn on z's lane and completes it on a lane beyond the stretch z governs; it occupied z's lane for part of the act only.

scenarios.name: occasion_d3_outside
scenarios.narrative: x drove along z's lane, left the governed stretch, and only afterwards, on a lane no zone sign governs, makes its U-turn: it was in the zone before the act began only.

scenarios.name: occasion_d5
scenarios.narrative: U-turn on z's lane; no ru.child is within p.child_presence_reach at the first observations of the act, then a child walks up beside the lane before the act is recognized; the other alternatives fail throughout.

scenarios.name: occasion_d5_outside
scenarios.narrative: Children stood beside z's lane before the act began and left; at every observation of the U-turn none lies within p.child_presence_reach; the other alternatives fail.

scenarios.name: occasion_d8

scenarios.name: occasion_d8_outside
scenarios.narrative: No beacon governs the region x occupied before the act; a non-flashing beacon governs every region x occupies during the U-turn and asm.pupils_in_class holds throughout it; children present.

scenarios.name: occasion_d10
scenarios.narrative: A beacon governs z's lane and asm.pupils_in_class holds throughout; the beacon is not flashing for the first part of the U-turn and flashing for the rest; children present.

scenarios.name: occasion_d10_outside
scenarios.narrative: A beacon governs z's lane and asm.pupils_in_class holds throughout; the beacon was flashing before the act and is not flashing at any observation of the U-turn; children present.

scenarios.name: occasion_d12
scenarios.narrative: No beacon governs the region x occupies at the start of the U-turn, a flashing beacon governs the region it ends on; z's conditions do not hold throughout; children present, school in session, inside the margin.

scenarios.name: occasion_d12_outside
scenarios.narrative: A beacon governed the region x occupied before the act; no beacon governs any region x occupies or z governs during the U-turn; z's conditions do not hold throughout; children present.

scenarios.name: occasion_d13
scenarios.narrative: No beacon; env.civil_time leaves z's posted window during the U-turn, so z's conditions do not hold for the first part of the act and hold for the rest; children present, school in session, inside the margin.

scenarios.name: occasion_d13_outside
scenarios.narrative: No beacon; z's conditions held before the act and do not hold at any observation of the U-turn; children present.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: x makes a U-turn on z's lane with children present while asm.school_not_in_session_day is declared true at every observation of the act.

under_way.justification: An observation inside the act is one within the U-turn window behind the recognition at which x's heading is changing (drv.motion.yawing: "the absolute value of its yaw rate exceeds yaw_floor", kin.yaw_rate): the turning is motion, and x occupied the zone's lanes before the turning began, so no region alone tells the act apart.

param_proposals.name: p.u_turn_window
param_proposals.convention: U-turn recognition window: the longest time over which a reversal of heading, made in one movement or in several forward and backing movements, is recognized as one turning; a multi-point turn on a narrow street.
param_proposals.source: observed durations of three-point turns (naturalistic driving studies)

param_proposals.name: p.u_turn_reversal_tolerance
param_proposals.convention: Reversal tolerance: the largest difference between the size of the heading change over the window and a half turn within which the road user counts as proceeding in the opposite direction; covers the offset of a turn into a lane of the opposite direction and heading noise.
param_proposals.source: trajectory-classification practice for U-turn detection

param_proposals.name: p.yaw_rate_resolution
param_proposals.convention: Sensor resolution: the smallest yaw rate the acquisition standard separates from a straight path; a yaw rate at or below it counts as no heading change.
param_proposals.source: yaw-rate resolution of the carla_scene_graph acquisition standard

param_proposals.name: p.child_presence_reach
param_proposals.convention: Presence reach: the ground distance from a child's body to a travel region of a school zone within which the child counts as present in the zone; the width of a sidewalk and verge beside the roadway.
param_proposals.source: urban street cross-section conventions (sidewalk and buffer widths)

segmentation.text: If the driver of a vehicle
intends to turn
at an intersection
and:
The turn is a right turn,
both the approach for the right turn and the right turn must be made from the right turn lane
if the highway has a right turn lane
as set forth in subsection 4 of NRS 484B.223 [NRS-484B-223-4a, NRS-484B-223-4b],
or must be made from the extreme right lane.

elements.justification: 'vehicle' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle ("every device in, upon or by which any person or property is or may be transported or drawn upon a highway"), claimed by id. 'the driver of' is a role read through the vehicle's controlled motion (observable_reading agency).

The intersection the intention is declared at and the turn is made in: st.intersection ("the region where two roadways meet"), entered by x (drv.motion.entering_region: "its footprint overlaps r (rel.occupies) at the observation and did not at the observation before") from the approach carrier it occupies whose entrance end is i (st.lane_enters: "the intersection region a directed approach carrier runs into at its entrance end").

The turn made is a right turn where the heading change of x since it entered i (drv.motion.heading_change_since_entry: "The signed heading change of road user x since its footprint last began to overlap region r, in degrees, left positive", from kin.yaw_rate) reaches the turn recognition angle to the right. The concept is 'not' a turn by itself; the rule compares it with its bound.

The approach for the turn and the turn are made from the right turn lane R where x's footprint overlaps R (rel.occupies) at its entry into i and at every observation of the approach length of path travelled before it at which x occupies a carrier entering i (a .path window, which reads kin.path_length, "distance travelled along the body's path"). R is the st.turn_lane ("a lane designated only for turning; side ∈ {left, right}") of side right that enters i (st.lane_enters).

The highway has a right turn lane as subsection 4 of NRS 484B.223 sets forth, whose words are borrowed: NRS-484B-223-4a and NRS-484B-223-4b both quote "a single right lane to be used only for turning". That is a st.turn_lane ("a lane designated only for turning") of side right, entering i (st.lane_enters), lying on the same highway (st.on_way: "the public way (a highway region) a structure region lies on"; st.highway) as the carrier x approached through, and serving x's direction: its designated direction (st.lane_direction) not opposed to that carrier's (drv.road.opposed_directions false), so that a turn lane on the opposing approach of the same way is not read.

intentions.meaning: The source's current plan for the road user includes a turn, to either hand, at the target region.

compositions.quote: a single right lane to be used only for turning
compositions.why: It borrows only the description of the lane, a single right lane to be used only for turning, to say which lane counts as a right turn lane here; whether a vehicle in that lane complies with paragraph (4)(a), driving in it only to turn right, decides nothing in this duty, so that rule need not apply, hold or be complied with.

compositions.quote: a single right lane to be used only for turning
compositions.why: It borrows only the same description of the lane; whether a vehicle in that lane complies with paragraph (4)(b), not travelling through the intersection, decides nothing in this duty, so that rule need not apply, hold or be complied with.

applicability: x carries ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle; at the observation x's right turn in intersection i is recognized: the heading change since x's latest entry into i (drv.motion.heading_change_since_entry(x, i) with step p.heading_since_step_carla_scene_graph) is at most minus p.turn_recognition_angle there and was not at the observation before; the source declared int.turn for x at i at the observation of that entry (Formula.intent, read through a past operator); and the highway has a right turn lane for x's approach: x entered i from a carrier c with st.lane_enters(c, i) lying on a highway h (st.on_way(c, h)), and some st.turn_lane R of side right enters i (st.lane_enters(R, i)), lies on h (st.on_way(R, h)) and has a designated direction not opposed to c's (drv.road.opposed_directions(R, c) with p.opposed_carriers_cosine false).
obligation: At the observation of that entry into i (read through a past operator), x's footprint overlaps such a lane R, and at every observation of the path window of length p.turn_approach_length behind the entry (measured in x's path, kin.path_length) at which x occupies a carrier entering i, it occupies that R: both the approach and the turn are made from the right turn lane.

narrowings.why: 'the driver of a vehicle' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion.

'the approach for the right turn' is read as the stretch of path, of the approach length, just before the entry into the intersection, during which every carrier of the intersection x is on must be the right turn lane; a lane change into the turn lane earlier than that stretch complies.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: x (ru.motor_vehicle) approaches i on a through lane c of highway h whose approach also has a right st.turn_lane R entering i; int.turn is declared for x at i; x enters i from c and turns right beyond p.turn_recognition_angle.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: Same highway; x, with int.turn declared at i, is on R for the whole approach length before its entry, enters i from R and turns right.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: x, with int.turn declared at i, turns left in i (heading change positive beyond p.turn_recognition_angle).

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: x turns right in i from a through lane with int.turn declared, but the source does not record which intersection the turn lane beside it enters, so whether the highway has a right turn lane for this approach is unknown.

param_proposals.name: p.turn_recognition_angle
param_proposals.convention: Turn recognition: the heading change through an intersection beyond which a passage counts as a turn rather than a straight crossing; half the right angle of a turn at a right-angled junction, leaving room for skewed junctions and lane offsets.
param_proposals.source: intersection geometry design conventions (AASHTO Green Book)

param_proposals.name: p.opposed_carriers_cosine
param_proposals.convention: Direction tolerance: minus the cosine of the narrowest angle between two carriers' designated directions that counts as opposite directions; carriers within about 45 degrees of exactly opposed count.
param_proposals.source: road-network direction conventions of map data

param_proposals.name: p.turn_approach_length
param_proposals.convention: Turn approach: the distance travelled just before entering an intersection over which a turning vehicle's approach is judged; about two passenger-car lengths, shorter than the storage of a short turn bay.
param_proposals.source: AASHTO Green Book turn-lane storage practice

both the approach for the right turn and the right turn must be made from the right turn lane
if the highway has a right turn lane

or must be made from the extreme right lane.

segmentation.text: A signal of intention to turn right or left, or otherwise turn a vehicle from a direct course, shall be given continuously during not less than the last 100 feet traveled
in a business or residential district
and not less than the last 300 feet traveled
in any other area
prior to changing the course
of a vehicle.
This rule shall be observed, regardless of the weather.

elements.justification: A signal of intention to turn is the signal itself, not a declared intention (the ontology: "a signal 'of intention' is the signal"): sig.turn_indicator ("the turn indicator state ∈ {off, left, right}") or sig.hand_signal ("a driver's or rider's arm signal; meaning ∈ {no_signal, left, right, stop_or_slow, re_enter}") showing the side of the change of course; sig.turn_indicator is 'not a stand-in' for the turn itself, which is read separately. A direct course is travel along the designated direction of the carrier x occupies (rel.occupies a st.travel_region carrying st.lane_direction); turning right or left or otherwise from it is x's velocity departing to one side of that direction, the proposed concepts drv.motion.veering_left and drv.motion.veering_right ("it moves forward along the carrier while its velocity points to the left [right] of the carrier's direction by more than a tolerance", from kin.velocity and kin.speed); following a bend of the carrier is not a departure, since the designated direction bends with it. 'given continuously during not less than the last 100 feet traveled' is a window measured in distance travelled (a .path window, which reads kin.path_length: "distance travelled along the body's path since the start of the trace, monotone") at every observation of which the signal of the departure's side is shown; the figure is the law's literal.
The same .path window (kin.path_length) with the law's other literal, the bound selected where the place is not in a business or residence district (span f7).

Changing the course is the observation at which a departure to one side begins: drv.motion.veering_left or drv.motion.veering_right holds for a carrier x occupies (rel.occupies) and held for none at the observation before. The signal window ends there.

'vehicle' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle ("every device in, upon or by which any person or property is or may be transported or drawn upon a highway"), claimed by id: the subject x whose course changes.
