segmentation.text: Upon any highway
outside of a business or residence district
no person shall stop, park or leave standing
any vehicle, whether attended or unattended,
upon the paved or main-traveled part of the highway
when it is practicable to stop, park or so leave such vehicle off such part of the highway,
but in every event
an unobstructed width of the highway
opposite a standing vehicle
shall be left for the free passage of other vehicles
and
a clear view of such stopped vehicles shall be available from a distance of 200 feet in each direction upon such highway.

This section shall not apply to the driver of any vehicle which is disabled while on the paved or main-traveled portion of a highway in such manner and to such extent that it is impossible to avoid stopping and temporarily leaving such disabled vehicle in such position.

elements.justification: st.highway: "the entire public way between its boundary lines, including sidewalks and shoulders" (DEF-NRS-484A-095, "the entire width between the boundary lines of every way"); x is upon it where its footprint overlaps it (rel.occupies).

'stop', prohibited here, takes DEF-NRS-484A-260 ("any halting, even momentarily, of a vehicle, whether occupied or not, except when necessary to avoid conflict with other traffic or in compliance with the directions of a police officer or official traffic-control device"); 'park' (DEF-NRS-484A-155, "the standing of a vehicle") and 'leave standing' (DEF-NRS-484A-250, "the halting of a vehicle") are halts too. The halt is drv.motion.halted ("speed ... at or below speed_floor ... with no minimum duration", kin.speed), which observes any halting, even momentary. The definition's exclusions are carried beside it: a halt behind another road user ahead in the same lane (rel.ahead_behind_in_lane) within the conflict standoff gap (rel.surface_gap) avoids a conflict; a halt while a police officer's stop direction (dev.human_direction, indication stop) or a signal showing a red indication or a stop sign (dev.traffic_signal, dev.stop_sign) governs (dev.governs) the travel region x occupies is in compliance with directions. Purposes of parking and standing (loading, passengers) are not observable and are read through the halt (observable_reading purpose).
'vehicle' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle, claimed by id; 'whether attended or unattended' excludes no member.

The paved or main-traveled part of the highway is the st.roadway ("the part of a highway improved for vehicular traffic, excluding shoulder"; DEF-NRS-484A-220, "that portion of a highway which is improved and ordinarily used for vehicular traffic, exclusive of the shoulder"); x halts upon it where its footprint overlaps it (rel.occupies). A paved shoulder is off it: the words set the main-traveled part against the part off it where the vehicle may be left. st.roadway is 'not a stand-in' for the sidewalk.

A vehicle disabled on the roadway so that stopping cannot be avoided is read through its nearest observables, the same as the earlier mapping of 'a disabled vehicle' in this iteration: its engine or motor not running, so that propulsion is unavailable (kin.engine_running: "the vehicle's engine or motor is running, so that propulsion is available", false), with its hazard lamps flashing (sig.hazard: "both indicators flashing together"), while it occupies the roadway (rel.occupies, st.roadway). kin.engine_running is 'not a stand-in' for motion or a halt, and is not used as either; the gap records that the disability itself has no atom.

operationalizations.standard: practicable to stop, park or so leave such vehicle off such part of the highway
operationalizations.convention: Off-road stopping convention: moving off the main-traveled part is practicable where a shoulder lies within the reach of a short lateral move from the halted vehicle's body; the ground distance from the body to the nearest shoulder is the measured magnitude compared with the reach.

assumptions.meaning: The place of the observation lies inside a business district or a residence district declared for the map or the trace.

applicability: x carries ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle; at the observation x's footprint overlaps a st.highway (rel.occupies) and asm.within_business_or_residence_district does not hold; and x is not disabled there: not (kin.engine_running false and sig.hazard on while x occupies a st.roadway).
obligation: It is not the case that, at the observation, x is halted (drv.motion.halted with p.speed_resolution) with its footprint overlapping a st.roadway, while some st.shoulder lies within p.offroad_stop_reach of x's body (st.region_geometry distance), unless the halt falls under the exclusions of the defined 'stop': some other road user is ahead of x in the same lane (rel.ahead_behind_in_lane) with a surface gap (rel.surface_gap) at most p.stopping_conflict_gap, or a dev.human_direction with indication stop, a dev.traffic_signal displaying circular_red, a red_arrow or flashing_red, or a dev.stop_sign governs (dev.governs) a travel region x occupies.

narrowings.why: 'stop, park or leave standing' are read through the halt itself; the purposes that set parking and standing apart (loading, receiving passengers) are not observable, and every halt is a stop under the definition that applies, so none is lost.
'practicable' is read through the distance to a shoulder only; the shoulder's width, surface and load-bearing are not read.

A clear view of it from a distance along the highway is st.sight_distance at its place: "the distance along the road within which a vehicle at a point and another vehicle on the road could see each other ... both the view of approaching traffic from that point and its being seen by drivers approaching it"; it is at least the law's literal. It is 'not a stand-in' for whether an actual road user saw x (rel.visible), and is not used as one.

A vehicle disabled on the roadway is read through its nearest observables, as in the first obligation of this line: engine or motor not running (kin.engine_running: "so that propulsion is available", false) with hazard lamps flashing (sig.hazard: "both indicators flashing together"), while it occupies the roadway (rel.occupies, st.roadway). kin.engine_running is 'not a stand-in' for motion or a halt; the gap records that the disability itself has no atom.

obligation: The sight distance at x's place (st.sight_distance) is at least the literal of span g12.

narrowings.why: 'in each direction' is read through the sight distance the source reports for the place, which states both the view from it and its being seen along the road without separating the two directions of the way.

segmentation.text: A person shall not stop, stand or park
a vehicle,
except when necessary to avoid conflict with
other traffic
or in compliance with law
or the directions of a police officer or official traffic-control device,
in any of the following places:
Within an intersection.

elements.justification: 'stop', prohibited here, takes DEF-NRS-484A-260 ("any halting, even momentarily, of a vehicle, whether occupied or not"), whose exclusions the law's own spans h3 to h6 restate; 'stand' (DEF-NRS-484A-250, "the halting of a vehicle") and 'park' (DEF-NRS-484A-155, "the standing of a vehicle") are halts too. The halt is drv.motion.halted (kin.speed at or below the resolution, "with no minimum duration"), observing any halting, even momentary. 'A person' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion (observable_reading agency); the purposes setting parking and standing apart are read through the halt (observable_reading purpose).
'vehicle' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle, claimed by id.
'other traffic' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic ("pedestrians, ridden or herded animals, vehicles and other conveyances"), every member other than x.

A halt in compliance with law is a halt some rule requires. The nearest observables are those of the commonest such halt inside an intersection, yielding to an emergency vehicle showing its warning lamps or sounding its siren (ru.emergency_vehicle with sig.warning_lamp flashing or rotating, or sig.siren); ru.emergency_vehicle is 'not a stand-in' for a responding vehicle, which is why its lamp or siren is read. The gap records that no operator reads whether any rule requires the halt.

The directions of a police officer: dev.human_direction ("a person directing traffic and the direction given; role ∈ {police_officer, ...}; indication ∈ {stop, ...}") with role police_officer and indication stop; of an official traffic-control device: a dev.traffic_signal displaying circular_red, a red_arrow or flashing_red, or a dev.stop_sign; either governing (dev.governs) the intersection x occupies or the carrier it entered through (st.lane_enters, rel.occupies). The device's presence is the evidence of its official status (observable_reading status).

Within an intersection: x's footprint overlaps (rel.occupies) a st.intersection ("the region where two roadways meet"; DEF-NRS-484A-105). st.intersection is 'not a stand-in' for a crosswalk or a stop line, which are not read.

operationalizations.standard: necessary to avoid conflict
operationalizations.convention: Conflict-standoff convention: a halt is necessary to avoid a conflict where another member of traffic lies ahead of the halted vehicle (the longitudinal component of rel.bearing positive, in the vehicle's frame) at a surface gap no greater than a queue spacing at standstill; the measured gap is compared with the bound.

applicability: x carries ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle and at the observation its footprint overlaps an intersection i (rel.occupies, st.intersection).
obligation: It is not the case that x is halted (drv.motion.halted with p.speed_resolution) at the observation, unless: some road user other than x carrying ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic lies ahead of x (rel.bearing longitudinal component positive) at a surface gap (rel.surface_gap) at most p.stopping_conflict_gap; or a ru.emergency_vehicle showing sig.warning_lamp flashing or rotating or sounding sig.siren is in the scene; or a dev.human_direction of role police_officer with indication stop, a dev.traffic_signal displaying circular_red, a red_arrow or flashing_red, or a dev.stop_sign governs (dev.governs) i or the carrier x entered i through.

narrowings.why: 'A person' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion; the purposes that set standing and parking apart from stopping are not observable and every halt is read as a stop.
'official' is read through the device's presence on the road.

gaps.proposal: `Formula.haltRequired (subject)` — true at an observation where some rule of the set, engaged for the subject there, is complied with only if the subject is halted; decides whether a halt was made in compliance with law, the action the law requires, which the exception 'in compliance with law' turns on and which no single composed rule names

contract: Road user x has entered structure region r and has not since stood clear of it by clearance: x entered r (drv.motion.entering_region: its footprint overlaps r at that observation and did not at the observation before) at the observation or at an earlier one, and at every observation from that entry up to the observation the ground distance from x's body outline to r (st.region_geometry, m, world frame; zero while the footprint overlaps r) has stayed below clearance. It becomes true at an entry, holds while x stays on r or within clearance of it, becomes false at the first observation at which x's body stands at clearance or more from r, and stays false until x's next entry. Unknown where it is undecided whether x entered r at an observation since which the distance stayed below clearance (at x's first observation, whether it entered there is unknown), or where the distance is unobserved at an observation that decides it. Not denoted: the side of r on which the body stands (a body that backs out of r and stays within clearance of it still holds), x's direction or speed, or a halt: the caller reads those.

params.name: clearance
params.meaning: the ground distance from x's body outline to r at or beyond which x counts as clear of r; the caller passes the distance its words state

elements.span: x entered r (drv.motion.entering_region: its footprint overlaps r at that observation and did not at the observation before)
elements.justification: The entry is the co-proposed concept drv.motion.entering_region, whose contract is “Road user x enters structure region r at the observation: its footprint overlaps r (rel.occupies) at the observation and did not at the observation before”; it is the event from which the state is counted, and the formula's past operator (since) reads it at the observation it occurred. rel.occupies is the atom the entry reads: “a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region”.

elements.span: the ground distance from x's body outline to r (st.region_geometry, m, world frame; zero while the footprint overlaps r)
elements.justification: st.region_geometry carries “the ground distance from a road user's body outline to it (zero when they overlap)”. Not a stand-in for occupancy: the state does not read the distance as occupancy; the entry is read through rel.occupies, and the distance only decides when the body stands clear.

scenarios.name: holds
scenarios.narrative: x does not overlap r at its first observations and stands farther than clearance from it; its footprint overlaps r from the third observation; at the sixth it has left r and its body outline stands at a distance below clearance from r. At the sixth observation the concept holds.

scenarios.name: fails
scenarios.narrative: x enters r at the third observation, leaves it at the fifth, and at the eighth its body outline stands at clearance or more from r. At the eighth observation the concept fails, and it stays false at the later observations at which x does not enter r again.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: As holds, but the source maps r without its outline, so the distance from x's body to r is unobserved at the sixth observation, where x no longer overlaps r.

contract: The distance road user x would cover from the observation to a standstill if it kept its present speed for reaction_time and then slowed at the constant deceleration deceleration: its speed (kin.speed, m/s) times reaction_time, plus the square of its speed divided by twice deceleration; in metres, zero for a body at a standstill. Not denoted: the distance x actually covers before a later halt, the deceleration the surface, the grade or the vehicle allows (the caller passes deceleration), whether anything lies within the distance, or whether x is required to stop.

params.name: reaction_time
params.meaning: the time over which x keeps its speed before braking begins

params.name: deceleration
params.meaning: the constant deceleration at which x slows once braking begins; strictly positive

elements.justification: kin.speed is the “magnitude of velocity” in m/s, the one measured input of the distance. Not a stand-in for acceleration: the deceleration is the caller's parameter, never read from kin.accel_longitudinal.

literals.why: the factor of uniformly decelerated motion: a body slowing at constant deceleration from a speed covers the square of the speed divided by twice the deceleration

scenarios.name: holds
scenarios.narrative: x moves at a steady speed; the instance fixes reaction_time and deceleration, and its bounds bracket the speed times reaction_time plus the squared speed over twice deceleration: the value lies in the bounds.

scenarios.name: fails
scenarios.narrative: x moves at a higher steady speed with the same instance parameters and the same bounds: the computed distance lies above the upper bound.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: As holds, but the source does not observe x's speed at the observation.

segmentation.text: It is unlawful for the driver of any vehicle:
When crossing at grade any track or tracks of a railroad,

to fail to completely cross the track or tracks without stopping due to insufficient: (1) Space for the vehicle on the opposite side of the railroad crossing; or (2) Undercarriage clearance of the vehicle.

As used in this section, “completely cross” means to travel across a railroad track or tracks in such a manner that the trailing end of the vehicle is 15 feet or more past the nearest rail of the railroad track or tracks.

elements.justification: “vehicle” is the term DEF-NRS-484A-320 defines, admitted as DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle, so it is claimed as one atom, ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle: “membership of a legal aggregate: the atom's literal argument is an aggregate id”; the reading classifies the classes under it by the definition's words “every device in, upon or by which any person or property is or may be transported or drawn upon a highway, except: (1) Devices moved by human power or used exclusively upon stationary rails; (2) Electric bicycles; ... (4) An electric scooter”, so its exclusions are the reading's and are not expanded here. Its exclusion “a relational role such as who drives or controls a vehicle” does not apply: “driver” (DEF-NRS-484A-080, “every person who drives or is in actual physical control of a vehicle”) is not read as membership but through the vehicle's controlled motion (the agency reading on s1).

“crossing at grade any track or tracks of a railroad” is a level crossing: st.railway_crossing is the “level crossing of a railway with the roadway, and its nearest rail”; “railroad” (DEF-NRS-484A-200) is “a carrier of persons or property upon cars, other than streetcars, operated upon stationary rails”, and the atom's word “railway” already leaves out a streetcar line laid in the street, which is not a railway level crossing, so no further condition is needed. The subject is crossing from its entry onto the crossing (drv.motion.entering_region, over rel.occupies: “a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region”) until it has completely crossed it, which is drv.position.within_clearance_since_entry(x, r) with the clearance s4 states: the concept reads st.region_geometry, “the ground distance from a road user's body outline to it”. The crossing r is the subject's own: anchored by rel.occupies at the entry and by the distance since, never any crossing of the scene.

“to fail to completely cross ... without stopping”: “stopping” is DEF-NRS-484A-260, “any halting, even momentarily, of a vehicle, whether occupied or not, except when necessary to avoid conflict with other traffic or in compliance with the directions of a police officer or official traffic-control device”. The halting is drv.motion.halted, “A road user is at a standstill at the observation ... the road user's speed (kin.speed, m/s) is at or below speed_floor ... with no minimum duration”, which keeps “even momentarily”; its own definition id (DEF-NRS-484A-255) is a required stop, but its contract denotes a standstill at an observation whatever the duty, which is what this halting is. A halt while the vehicle is crossing and has not completely crossed is the failure. The definition's exception for a direction of a police officer is carried beside it: dev.human_direction is “a person directing traffic and the direction given; role ∈ {police_officer, ...}; indication ∈ {stop, ...}”, tied to the subject by dev.governs (“the travel regions whose traffic the device controls”) on a travel region (st.travel_region) the subject's footprint overlaps (rel.occupies); dev.governs is not a stand-in for a position, and it is not read as one: it says which road users the direction is given to. The other parts of the definition's exception are read as the narrowings on s3 say.

The section's own definition of “completely cross”: “the trailing end of the vehicle is 15 feet or more past the nearest rail”. Once the body has left the crossing, the point of its outline nearest the crossing is its trailing end, so “trailing end ... 15 feet or more past” is the ground distance from the body outline to the crossing region (st.region_geometry: “the ground distance from a road user's body outline to it (zero when they overlap)”) at or above the literal 15 ft; drv.position.within_clearance_since_entry with clearance 15 ft is true from the entry until that first holds. st.railway_crossing carries the crossing “and its nearest rail”; rel.occupies anchors the entry.

applicability: x is a vehicle (ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle), and there is a railway level crossing r (st.railway_crossing) that x is crossing and has not completely crossed: drv.position.within_clearance_since_entry(x, r) with clearance the literal 15 ft of s4 — x's footprint entered r (drv.motion.entering_region, over rel.occupies) at the observation or earlier, and at every observation since its body outline has stood less than 15 ft from r (st.region_geometry distance; zero while on r). Read at every observation.
obligation: At every observation at which the applicability holds, x is not halted: drv.motion.halted(x) with speed_floor p.speed_resolution is false (a single observation at a standstill is a halt, since stopping is “any halting, even momentarily”). A halt does not violate where it is in compliance with a police officer's direction: some human direction d (dev.human_direction) with role police_officer and indication stop governs (dev.governs) a travel region l (st.travel_region) x's footprint overlaps (rel.occupies) at that observation. The obligation reads x's motion and the direction governing the region x is on; it needs no crossing of its own.

narrowings.why: “the driver of any vehicle” is read through the vehicle's controlled motion: the vehicle crossing is taken to be driven, and the duty binds its conduct whoever or whatever is at the controls.

“due to insufficient: (1) Space for the vehicle on the opposite side of the railroad crossing; or (2) Undercarriage clearance of the vehicle” states why the vehicle stops; neither the room it would need beyond the crossing nor its undercarriage clearance over the crossing's profile is observable, so the cause is read through the conduct it explains: a halt while the vehicle is crossing and has not yet completely crossed. A halt on the crossing for another cause (a breakdown) is not told apart.

The posted definition of stopping excepts a halt “necessary to avoid conflict with other traffic”. This section makes a halt due to insufficient space for the vehicle on the opposite side — the space that queued traffic or an object fills — the failure it forbids; reading that exception into it would empty clause (1). The rule therefore does not excuse a halt on the crossing because a road user stands ahead of the vehicle. Of the exception for “the directions of a police officer or official traffic-control device”, the police officer's direction to stop is read; no official device directs a halt on the crossing itself (the railway signal or gate directs a halt before it, which a vehicle already crossing has passed, and a signal or stop sign beyond directs a halt at its own line, queueing for which on the tracks is clause (1)), so no device direction is read.

“the nearest rail” is read as the boundary of the crossing region the map carries (st.railway_crossing with its nearest rail): the distance is measured from the body outline to that region, which is at the rail or beyond it.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: A passenger car (a class the reading includes under DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle) drives along a roadway, enters a railway crossing r (st.railway_crossing with its outline) and, with a truck queued just beyond the crossing, halts with its footprint still overlapping r for several observations. No human direction is in the scene.

scenarios.narrative: The car enters the crossing, travels across it at a steady speed without halting, and halts only well after its body outline has stood more than 15 ft past the crossing region.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: The car drives on a roadway with no railway crossing in the scene and halts at a stop line.

scenarios.name: blind

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: The car crosses the rails, leaves the crossing region, and halts behind a queue with its trailing end a short distance past the crossing, less than 15 ft from it.

scenarios.name: branch_2
scenarios.narrative: The car halts on the crossing while a police officer (dev.human_direction, role police_officer, indication stop) governing the roadway the car occupies directs it to stop.

scenarios.name: branch_3
scenarios.narrative: No other road user is in the scene: the car crosses alone, its body outline reaches more than 15 ft past the crossing, and it halts there.

segmentation.text: It is unlawful for any person to drive or operate a vehicle of any kind or character
at: A rate of speed
greater than is reasonable or proper, having due regard for the traffic, surface and width of the highway, the weather and other highway conditions.

elements.justification: “a vehicle of any kind or character”: “vehicle” is DEF-NRS-484A-320, admitted as DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle and claimed as the one atom ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle (“membership of a legal aggregate”); “of any kind or character” adds no class beyond the definition's. Its exclusion “a relational role such as who drives or controls a vehicle” does not apply: “any person to drive or operate” is read through the vehicle's controlled motion, drv.motion.moving (“A road user is in motion at the observation: its speed exceeds speed_floor”, over kin.speed), since “a vehicle moving on the road is taken to be driven”.
“A rate of speed” is kin.speed, the “magnitude of velocity” in m/s; the bound it is held to is the operationalization of s3.

operationalizations.standard: a rate of speed greater than is reasonable or proper, having due regard for the traffic, surface and width of the highway, the weather and other highway conditions
operationalizations.convention: Assured clear distance and design-speed conventions: the stopping sight distance model (a perception-reaction time and a braking deceleration selected by the surface: dry, wet, icy) bounds speed by the sight distance along the road and by the visibility distance; the side-friction convention bounds the speed on a curve by a lateral acceleration; a speed-proportional lateral margin bounds the speed by the room the lane leaves beside the vehicle; a minimum time headway bounds the speed by the gap to traffic ahead in the lane. Each factor's magnitude enters its bound with the speed, so the bound moves with the factor's degree.

applicability: x is a vehicle (ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle) and is moving: drv.motion.moving(x) with speed_floor p.speed_resolution. Read at every observation.
obligation: Surrogate. x's speed v (kin.speed) is not greater than reasonable: every bound below holds at the observation. Let S be x's stopping distance drv.motion.stopping_distance(x; p.perception_reaction_time, a), the deceleration a selected by the surface with Term.cond: p.braking_decel_ice where env.ice_or_snow holds; else p.braking_decel_wet where env.wet_road or env.precipitation holds; else p.braking_decel_dry. (1) S is at most the sight distance at x's place (st.sight_distance). (2) S is at most the visibility distance (env.visibility). (3) v times v times the curvature at x's place (st.curvature) is at most p.curve_lateral_accel. (4) For every lane l (st.lane) x's footprint overlaps (rel.occupies): p.lateral_margin_time times v is at most the lane's width (st.lane_width) less x's width (kin.extent, width). (5) For every road user y of the scene that is not x (same) and is ahead of x in the same lane (rel.ahead_behind_in_lane): p.traffic_time_headway times v is at most the surface gap from x to y (rel.surface_gap).

narrowings.why: “any person to drive or operate” is read through the vehicle's controlled motion: a moving vehicle is taken to be driven or operated, and the duty binds its speed whoever or whatever is at the controls.

The traffic (DEF-NRS-484A-285, “pedestrians, ridden or herded animals, vehicles and other conveyances either singly or together using any highway for purposes of travel”) is read through every road user ahead of the subject in its own lane, whatever its class, by the time gap to it at the subject's speed: a road user in a lane of the highway ahead of the subject is one the speed must regard, so no class condition is read. Traffic crossing, oncoming or beside the road is not read.
The surface is read by a condition that selects the braking deceleration: icy or snow-covered, wet (or precipitation falling), otherwise dry; the degree of grip within each class is not read.

The width of the highway is read through the width of the lane the subject occupies against the subject's own width; the highway's whole width between its boundary lines (st.highway) is not read, and where the subject occupies no lane this factor sets no bound.
The weather is read through precipitation (selecting the wet deceleration) and the visibility distance (the stopping distance kept within it); wind and temperature are not read.

The catch-all “other highway conditions” is read only through the sight distance along the road and the curvature of the road at the subject's place; grade, darkness, crests and obstructions are not read.

scenarios.narrative: A passenger car moves on a dry straight lane in fog at a speed whose stopping distance exceeds the observed visibility distance; the sight distance is long and nothing is ahead in the lane.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: The car moves slowly on a dry straight lane of ample width with a long sight distance and visibility, alone in the scene: every bound holds.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: The car stands halted at the curb throughout the trace.

scenarios.name: blind

scenarios.name: branch_1

scenarios.name: branch_2

scenarios.name: branch_3
scenarios.narrative: The car follows another car ahead in the same lane at a surface gap shorter than the time headway at its speed.

scenarios.name: branch_4
scenarios.narrative: A wide truck moves in a narrow lane at a speed whose lateral margin exceeds the room the lane leaves beside it.

segmentation.text: An operator of a bicycle, an electric bicycle or an electric scooter
upon a roadway
shall give all signals by hand and arm
in the manner required by NRS 484B.420 [DEF-NRS-484B-420],
except that the operator may give a signal for a right turn by extending his or her right hand and arm horizontally and to the right side of the bicycle, electric bicycle or electric scooter.

elements.justification: The three terms are the admitted aggregates DEF-NRS-484A-025::bicycle (“a device propelled by human power upon which a person may ride”), DEF-NRS-484B-017::electric_bicycle (“a device upon which a person may ride, having two or three wheels ... an electric motor which produces not more than 750 watts”) and DEF-NRS-484B-018::electric_scooter (“a vehicle with handlebars and an electric motor”), each claimed as one ru.aggregate atom (“membership of a legal aggregate”), the same mapping the index records for “The operator of a bicycle, an electric bicycle or an electric scooter”. The exclusion “a relational role such as who drives or controls a vehicle” does not apply: “An operator” is read through the device's controlled motion (agency reading).

“roadway” is DEF-NRS-484A-220, “that portion of a highway which is improved and ordinarily used for vehicular traffic, exclusive of the shoulder”: st.roadway is “the part of a highway improved for vehicular traffic, excluding shoulder”, the definition's whole extent; “upon” is rel.occupies, “a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region”. The roadway is not a stand-in for the sidewalk, which the rule does not read as roadway.

“give all signals by hand and arm”: sig.hand_signal is “a driver's or rider's arm signal; meaning ∈ {no_signal, left, right, stop_or_slow, re_enter}”, whose meanings are exactly those NRS 484B.420 sets forth in the words s4 borrows: “(1) Left turn: Hand and arm extended horizontally. (2) Right turn: Hand and arm extended upward. (3) Stop or decrease speed: Hand and arm extended downward. (4) Reentering lane of traffic from parked position: Hand and arm extended horizontally.” A signal the rider gives otherwise is a lit turn indicator, sig.turn_indicator, “state ∈ {off, left, right}”; its exclusion (“the turn or lane change itself”) does not apply, since the rule reads the signal, not the turn. “all signals” is every signal the rider shows: where an indicator is lit, an arm signal of the same meaning must be given with it; where only an arm signal is given, it is given by hand and arm. Left horizontal serves both a left turn and reentering, so an indicator to the left is matched by either meaning.

The permitted right-turn form, “extending his or her right hand and arm horizontally and to the right side”, is an arm signal whose meaning is a right turn: sig.hand_signal records “the meaning of the one given”, so it reads right, as the form of NRS 484B.420 does; the exception admits it as a signal given in the required manner, and the rule accepts an arm signal of meaning right however it is formed.

compositions.quote: (1) Left turn: Hand and arm extended horizontally. (2) Right turn: Hand and arm extended upward. (3) Stop or decrease speed: Hand and arm extended downward. (4) Reentering lane of traffic from parked position: Hand and arm extended horizontally.

applicability: x is a member of DEF-NRS-484A-025::bicycle, DEF-NRS-484B-017::electric_bicycle or DEF-NRS-484B-018::electric_scooter (ru.aggregate); x's footprint overlaps a roadway (rel.occupies, st.roadway); and x gives a signal: its turn indicator (sig.turn_indicator) is left or right, or its arm signal (sig.hand_signal) is other than no_signal. Read at every observation.
obligation: x gives the signal by hand and arm: sig.hand_signal(x) is other than no_signal; where sig.turn_indicator(x) is left, sig.hand_signal(x) is left or re_enter; where sig.turn_indicator(x) is right, sig.hand_signal(x) is right (the posture of NRS 484B.420 or the right-arm form of the exception, both read as meaning right).

narrowings.why: “An operator” is read through the device's controlled motion: the rider of the bicycle, electric bicycle or electric scooter on the roadway is the one whose signals are judged, whoever is at the controls.

The manner of NRS 484B.420 is read through the meaning the source decodes from the arm signal: which arm is extended and on which side are not observed (sig.hand_signal records the meaning only), so an arm signal is taken as given in the required manner when its meaning is one of the four the section sets forth. “All signals” is read as every signal the rider shows, an arm signal or a lit turn indicator; hazard lamps are not read as a signal.

segmentation.text: Every vehicle
upon a highway
of this State,
subject to exceptions with respect to parked vehicles as stated in chapters 484A to 484E, inclusive, of NRS,
must display lighted lamps and illuminating devices
as respectively required in this chapter for different classes of vehicles:
(a) At any time from one-half hour after sunset to one-half hour before sunrise;
(b) At any other time when, because of insufficient light or unfavorable atmospheric conditions, persons and vehicles on the highway are not clearly discernible at a distance of 1,000 feet ahead;
and (c) When directed by an official traffic control device.

elements.justification: “vehicle” is DEF-NRS-484A-320, admitted as DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle, claimed as the one atom ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle (“membership of a legal aggregate”); the definition's exclusions (“Devices moved by human power ...; Electric bicycles; ...; An electric scooter”) are the reading's classification. The exclusion “a relational role such as who drives” does not arise: the duty binds the vehicle itself.

“highway” is DEF-NRS-484A-095, “the entire width between the boundary lines of every way dedicated to a public authority”: st.highway is “the entire public way between its boundary lines, including sidewalks and shoulders”, the definition's whole extent; it is not a stand-in for the roadway and is not narrowed to one. “upon” is rel.occupies, “a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region”, the mapping the index records for “Upon any highway”.

The exceptions the chapters state concern parked vehicles, whose lamps the chapter's parking-lamp provisions govern, not this duty to show lighted lamps on the road; a parked vehicle is read as a vehicle at a standstill (drv.motion.halted, “the road user's speed (kin.speed, m/s) is at or below speed_floor”) whose engine is not running (kin.engine_running, “the vehicle's engine or motor is running, so that propulsion is available”; its exclusion, motion or a halt, does not apply: the halt is read from drv.motion.halted and the engine only tells a parked vehicle from one halted in traffic). The duty does not apply to such a vehicle.

“display lighted lamps and illuminating devices”: sig.headlamp is the “headlamp state ∈ {off, low_beam, high_beam}”; the lamps are lighted where the state is low_beam or high_beam. sig.position_lamp (“the lamps a vehicle shows without its headlamps”) is not the duty: lamps a vehicle shows without its headlamps lit do not display the lighted headlamps the chapter requires of a vehicle moving at these times.

env.darkness is “insufficient natural light; the boundary relative to sunset and sunrise is a reading parameter”: it denotes the time from a boundary after sunset to a boundary before sunrise, which the clause fixes as the literal one-half hour. It is a natural-light condition of the scene, not a legal region class, so it is the atom and not an assumption.

env.visibility is the “visibility distance (fog, dust, smoke)”: persons and vehicles are not clearly discernible at a distance of 1,000 feet ahead where the visibility distance is below the literal 1,000 ft. “because of insufficient light or unfavorable atmospheric conditions” names the causes of that low visibility; it is read through the visibility distance they reduce (perception reading). It is not the sight distance of a place (st.sight_distance), which a bend or a crest limits whatever the light and air.

An official traffic control device directing lamps on is a regulatory sign governing the vehicle's place: dev.regulatory_sign is “a point regulation by catalogue code”, tied to the vehicle by dev.governs (“the travel regions whose traffic the device controls”) on a travel region (st.travel_region) the vehicle's footprint overlaps (rel.occupies). Its code list has no direction to display lamps, and “an attribute value not listed is an ontology change request”: the span is mapped to these nearest atoms with an atom gap.

residues.why: “of this State” names the jurisdiction whose law this is; the run applies Nevada's law to the highways of the maps it reads, so every highway the rule reads is one this State's law governs and the duty is the same whether or not the words are stated.

The class-specific lamp sets the chapter requires (headlamps, tail lamps, clearance lamps, by class of vehicle) are provisions not in this corpus; the rule reads the headlamps every vehicle moving at these times shows (narrowing on s5), and the class-by-class sets are not captured.

applicability: x is a vehicle (ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle); x's footprint overlaps a highway (rel.occupies, st.highway); x is not parked: not both halted (drv.motion.halted(x) with speed_floor p.speed_resolution) and with its engine not running (kin.engine_running false); and at least one of the times holds (the list (a); (b); and (c) names the times at which the duty arises, so any one of them suffices): (a) env.darkness, with its boundary the literal one-half hour after sunset and before sunrise; (b) the visibility distance env.visibility is below the literal 1,000 ft; (c) a regulatory sign d (dev.regulatory_sign) directing lamps on governs (dev.governs) a travel region l (st.travel_region) x's footprint overlaps (rel.occupies) — the gap of s9. Read at every observation.
obligation: x displays lighted lamps: sig.headlamp(x) is low_beam or high_beam.

narrowings.why: “parked vehicles” is read through the vehicle's observable state: a vehicle at a standstill with its engine not running counts as parked, and the reason it stands is not read.

“lighted lamps and illuminating devices as respectively required ... for different classes of vehicles” is read through the headlamps (low or high beam lit); the other lamps a class must show are not read, and a drawn trailer, which no atom tells apart from its combination, is held to headlamps like its combination.

“persons and vehicles on the highway are not clearly discernible at a distance of 1,000 feet ahead” is a perception; it is read through the visibility distance (env.visibility) below 1,000 ft, the observable evidence of what can be discerned through the air and light, whatever their cause.

segmentation.text: Whenever a motor vehicle is being operated
on the traveled portion of the highway, or shoulder adjacent thereto,
during the times specified in NRS 484D.100 [NRS-484D-100-1],
the driver shall use a distribution of light, or composite beam,
directed high enough and of sufficient intensity to reveal persons and vehicles at a safe distance in advance of the vehicle,
subject to the following requirements and limitations:
Whenever a driver of a vehicle
approaches an oncoming vehicle within 500 feet,
the driver shall use a distribution of light, or composite beam, so aimed that the glaring rays are not projected into the eyes of the oncoming driver.
The lowermost distribution of light, or composite beam, specified in
subsection 2 of NRS 484D.210 [DEF-NRS-484D-210-1-2]
shall be deemed to avoid glare at all times, regardless of road contour and loading.

elements.justification: “motor vehicle” is DEF-NRS-484A-130, “every vehicle which is self-propelled but not operated upon rails”, admitted as DEF-NRS-484A-130::motor_vehicle and claimed as the one atom ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-130::motor_vehicle; it is not replaced by ru.motor_vehicle. “is being operated” is read through the vehicle's controlled motion: it is moving (drv.motion.moving, “its speed exceeds speed_floor”, over kin.speed) or its engine is running (kin.engine_running, “the vehicle's engine or motor is running, so that propulsion is available”), which tells a vehicle halted in traffic from a parked one; the engine atom's exclusion, motion or a halt, does not apply since motion is read from drv.motion.moving.

“the traveled portion of the highway” is the part of the highway (DEF-NRS-484A-095) the words narrow to the part traffic travels on: st.roadway, “the part of a highway improved for vehicular traffic, excluding shoulder”; “or shoulder adjacent thereto” is st.shoulder, “the part of the highway beside the roadway not intended for vehicular traffic”. “on” is rel.occupies, “a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region”.

“use a distribution of light, or composite beam” is the beam the vehicle's headlamps show: sig.headlamp, “headlamp state ∈ {off, low_beam, high_beam}”; the low beam is the lowermost distribution, the high beam the uppermost. Which beam is required is bounded by the operationalization of t5.

operationalizations.standard: a distribution of light directed high enough and of sufficient intensity to reveal persons and vehicles at a safe distance in advance of the vehicle
operationalizations.convention: Stopping sight distance against headlamp reach: a safe distance in advance of the vehicle is its stopping distance (perception-reaction time and design braking deceleration); the low beam reveals persons and vehicles to the distance the multiple-beam equipment standard sets for the lowermost beam. Where the stopping distance at the vehicle's speed exceeds that reach, the beam that reveals farther, the high beam, is required; where the low beam's reach covers it, either beam suffices. The speed enters the bound, so the required beam moves with it.

applicability: x is a motor vehicle (ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-130::motor_vehicle) being operated: drv.motion.moving(x) with speed_floor p.speed_resolution, or kin.engine_running(x); x's footprint overlaps a roadway or a shoulder (rel.occupies with st.roadway or st.shoulder); it is one of the times NRS 484D.100 specifies: ruleApplies NRS_484D_100_1 with its binder x mapped to x; and the requirement of NRS_484D_215_1_o2 does not apply to x (exception: not ruleApplies NRS_484D_215_1_o2 with x mapped to x, i.e. no oncoming vehicle within 500 ft). Read at every observation.
obligation: Surrogate. x uses a beam: sig.headlamp(x) is low_beam or high_beam; and where x's stopping distance drv.motion.stopping_distance(x; p.perception_reaction_time, p.braking_decel_wet) is greater than p.low_beam_reveal_distance, sig.headlamp(x) is high_beam.

narrowings.why: “is being operated” is read through the vehicle's controlled motion: moving, or standing with its engine running, whoever or whatever is at the controls.
“the driver shall use” is read through the vehicle's headlamp state: the beam the vehicle shows is the one its driver uses.

The aim and intensity of the beam are not observed; they are read through the headlamp state, the high beam revealing farther than the low beam. The safe distance is read as the stopping distance at the vehicle's speed under the design deceleration; where even the high beam's reach falls short of it, the rule asks no more than the high beam, the farthest-reaching distribution a vehicle carries.

segmentation.text: Whenever a motor vehicle is being operated
on the traveled portion of the highway, or shoulder adjacent thereto,
during the times specified in NRS 484D.100 [NRS-484D-100-1],
the driver shall use a distribution of light, or composite beam,
directed high enough and of sufficient intensity to reveal persons and vehicles at a safe distance in advance of the vehicle,
subject to the following requirements and limitations:
Whenever a driver of a vehicle
approaches an oncoming vehicle within 500 feet,
the driver shall use a distribution of light, or composite beam, so aimed that the glaring rays are not projected into the eyes of the oncoming driver.
The lowermost distribution of light, or composite beam, specified in
subsection 2 of NRS 484D.210 [DEF-NRS-484D-210-1-2]
shall be deemed to avoid glare at all times, regardless of road contour and loading.

elements.justification: The requirement is one of the “requirements and limitations” the line places on the motor vehicle being operated, so the subject is that vehicle: “motor vehicle” is DEF-NRS-484A-130, “every vehicle which is self-propelled but not operated upon rails”, admitted as DEF-NRS-484A-130::motor_vehicle and claimed as one ru.aggregate atom. “is being operated” is read through the vehicle's controlled motion: drv.motion.moving (“its speed exceeds speed_floor”, over kin.speed) or kin.engine_running (“the vehicle's engine or motor is running”); the engine atom's exclusion, motion or a halt, does not apply since motion is read from drv.motion.moving.

“the traveled portion of the highway” is st.roadway, “the part of a highway improved for vehicular traffic, excluding shoulder”; “or shoulder adjacent thereto” is st.shoulder, “the part of the highway beside the roadway not intended for vehicular traffic”; “on” is rel.occupies, “a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region”.

“a driver of a vehicle” names the same subject: the motor vehicle of t1 is a vehicle under DEF-NRS-484A-320 (“every device in, upon or by which any person or property is or may be transported or drawn upon a highway”), claimed as ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle. The exclusion “a relational role such as who drives or controls a vehicle” does not apply: “driver” is read through the vehicle's controlled motion (agency reading).

“an oncoming vehicle”: a road user y, other than x, of DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle (ru.aggregate; the definition excludes “Devices moved by human power”, “Electric bicycles” and “An electric scooter”, which the reading classifies) for which rel.oncoming holds: “headings opposed and closing”, with its tolerance p.oncoming_heading_cosine; “approaches” is the closing the relation requires. Its exclusion, the direction a road user approaches an intersection from, does not apply: the words relate the two vehicles' headings on the road, not an approach to an intersection. “within 500 feet” is the surface gap between the two bodies (rel.surface_gap, “distance between the nearest points of two bodies”) at or below the literal 500 ft.

“use a distribution of light, or composite beam, so aimed that the glaring rays are not projected into the eyes of the oncoming driver”: sig.headlamp, “headlamp state ∈ {off, low_beam, high_beam}”. The aim is not observed; the high beam, the uppermost distribution, is read as projecting glaring rays into the oncoming driver's eyes, and the low beam is deemed not to (t10 to t12). Headlamps off use no distribution of light and do not meet the duty to use one.

“The lowermost distribution of light, or composite beam” is the beam the words borrow from NRS 484D.210(2): “There shall be a lowermost distribution of light, or composite beam, so aimed and of sufficient intensity to reveal persons and vehicles at a distance of at least 100 feet ahead; and on a straight, level road under any condition of loading none of the high-intensity portion of the beam shall be directed to strike the eyes of an approaching driver.” It is the low beam of sig.headlamp (“state ∈ {off, low_beam, high_beam}”), which the rule accepts as compliant.

“shall be deemed to avoid glare at all times, regardless of road contour and loading”: where sig.headlamp is low_beam, the duty of t9 is met whatever the road's contour and the vehicle's loading, so neither is read.

compositions.quote: There shall be a lowermost distribution of light, or composite beam, so aimed and of sufficient intensity to reveal persons and vehicles at a distance of at least 100 feet ahead; and on a straight, level road under any condition of loading none of the high-intensity portion of the beam shall be directed to strike the eyes of an approaching driver.

applicability: x is a motor vehicle (ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-130::motor_vehicle; it is thereby a vehicle, ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle) being operated: drv.motion.moving(x) with speed_floor p.speed_resolution, or kin.engine_running(x); x's footprint overlaps a roadway or a shoulder (rel.occupies with st.roadway or st.shoulder); it is one of the times NRS 484D.100 specifies: ruleApplies NRS_484D_100_1 with its binder x mapped to x; and some road user y, not x (same), a member of DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle (ru.aggregate), is oncoming to x (rel.oncoming(x, y) with tolerance p.oncoming_heading_cosine) at a surface gap (rel.surface_gap(x, y)) at or below the literal 500 ft. Read at every observation.
obligation: x uses the lowermost beam: sig.headlamp(x) is low_beam.

narrowings.why: “a driver of a vehicle” is read through the vehicle's controlled motion: the vehicle approaching is the one whose beam is judged.

“the eyes of the oncoming driver” and the aim of the glaring rays are not observable; they are read through the headlamp state: the high beam is read as projecting glaring rays toward the oncoming vehicle, the low beam as deemed by the words not to, and the oncoming vehicle stands for its driver.
